# Your photo vault app lost your photos: what to do now

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/photo-vault-lost-photos
Last updated: 2026-11-11

Guide · Missing photos
## Your photo vault app lost your photos: what to do now
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 11 November 2026
Short answer
Stop and don't delete, reinstall or reset anything yet. Photos that vanish from a vault app are often still on the old phone, in the app's own cloud, or in a backup, and reinstalling can erase the last local copy. Check those places in order, then contact the developer with your app version and what happened.
Lost or missing photos are one of the most common complaints about vault apps. In the most recent one- and two-star App Store reviews of eight popular vault apps, which we read in October 2026, missing photos came up 47 times. The good news: "missing" often means "not where you're looking". This guide walks through what to do, in order, without making things worse.
Locked out rather than missing photos? See how to unlock a photo vault when you forgot the password .
### What should you not do when vault photos go missing?
Don't delete the app, reinstall it, or reset your iPhone. A vault app keeps its files inside its own storage on the phone. Deleting the app deletes that storage, and reinstalling gives you an empty vault. More in does deleting a vault app delete your photos?
- Don't delete or reinstall the vault app , on any device.
- Don't erase your old iPhone if you've just switched phones.
- Don't restore an older iPhone backup over your phone yet. It can replace newer data.
- Don't pay a "recovery" tool or service that promises to unlock a vault. If the vault really is encrypted, they can't; if it isn't, the developer can help for free.
### Where could the photos still be?
Check these places in order. Most recoveries happen at one of the first three.
- Inside the app, but somewhere else. Look for other albums or folders, a trash or "Recently Deleted" area, a second vault opened by a different PIN (a decoy you set up and forgot), or a filter that hides some items.
- On your old iPhone or iPad. If you switched phones, open the vault on the old device. Many vault apps don't move their photos with Quick Start or an iCloud backup.
- In the app's cloud or backup. Look in the app's settings for backup, sync or cloud. Some apps keep a cloud copy in their own service, which needs the same account you used before. Others back up to your own iCloud and restore when you open the vault with the same code on the same Apple Account.
- In your iCloud storage list. Go to Settings › [your name] › iCloud › Manage Account Storage and look for the vault app. If it's there with data, a backup exists, even if the app isn't showing it yet.
- On a computer. If the app's listing mentions iTunes, Finder or Wi-Fi transfer ( Private Photo Vault's does), connect the iPhone to a Mac or PC and check the app's files in Finder (iPhone › Files) or the Apple Devices app. Some apps keep copies there.
- In Photos. Check Collections › Utilities › Recently Deleted in the Photos app. If you deleted originals after importing them into the vault in the last 30 days, they may still be there.
### What happened? Match your situation
Common ways vault photos go missing, and where to look first
What happened Look first
Switched to a new iPhone The old iPhone, then the app's own backup or cloud restore
App was updated, then photos disappeared Force-quit and reopen; check for another update; contact the developer before reinstalling
Reinstalled the app The app's cloud or iCloud backup, signed in with the same account
Subscription ended Whether the app limits access on the free plan; resubscribing may restore access
Entered a different PIN or pattern You may be in a decoy vault; lock and try your main code
Only thumbnails show, or videos won't play Full-size files may still be downloading from the cloud; keep the app open on Wi-Fi
### How do you ask the developer for help?
Email the developer before you change anything else. Their contact details are on the app's App Store page under App Support, or in the app's settings. Include:
- The app name and version, and your iPhone model and iOS version.
- What you did just before the photos went missing (update, new phone, reinstall, subscription change).
- Roughly how many items are missing, and whether thumbnails show.
- Whether you used the app's cloud backup, and the account email if it has one.
Never send your PIN, password, pattern or recovery phrase. A real developer won't ask for it.
If the developer doesn't answer within a few days, you can ask Apple for a refund of a recent purchase at reportaproblem.apple.com. That won't recover photos, but it's worth knowing.
### How do you stop it happening again?
Use a vault with a backup you can restore, check that backup now and then, and keep your own copy of anything you can't replace.
- Know where your backup lives and what you need to restore it: an account, an Apple Account, a code, a recovery phrase.
- Check that backups finish. A full iCloud quietly stops them.
- Test a restore on another device if you can, before you need it.
- Export irreplaceable photos to an encrypted drive or a computer you control, as a second copy.
- Before switching phones, follow our new-iPhone checklist .
Noxium, which we make, was built around this problem. Its encrypted backup goes to your own iCloud on the free plan, and on a new iPhone you draw your pattern and the vault comes back. If you forget the pattern, the recovery phrase you wrote down at setup opens it. And if Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything.
Noxium backs up only encrypted data, to your own iCloud, and restores with your pattern.
A backup that actually restores
Noxium backs up an encrypted copy of your vault to your own iCloud, free. New phone? Draw your pattern and everything comes back.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Can deleted vault app photos be recovered?
Sometimes. If the app had a cloud backup, or you still have the old phone or a computer copy, yes. If the app kept photos only on the phone and the app was deleted, they're usually gone, because deleting an app deletes its storage.
Will reinstalling the vault app bring my photos back?
Only if the app restores them from a cloud backup. Reinstalling by itself gives you an empty vault, and it deletes any local copy that was left. Contact the developer first.
Does an iCloud backup of my iPhone include my vault photos?
It depends on the app. Some include their files in the iPhone's backup; many leave them out on purpose and use their own backup instead. Check the app's settings or ask the developer.
I see thumbnails but the photos won't open. Are they lost?
Not necessarily. Many vaults download full-size photos from the cloud in the background. Keep the app open on Wi-Fi and power for a while, and check your iCloud or the app's cloud storage isn't full.

# Keepsafe alternatives that don't need an account

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/keepsafe-alternatives
Last updated: 2026-11-13

Guide · Alternatives
## Keepsafe alternatives that don't need an account
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 13 November 2026
Short answer
If you want a Keepsafe alternative without an email account, look for a vault that says it needs no account and backs up to your own iCloud instead of its own servers. From their App Store listings in October 2026, Vaultaire, Obscura, Encamera and Noxium (which we make) all work without an account. Apple's Hidden album needs no extra account either, but it opens with your iPhone passcode.
Keepsafe is one of the best-known photo vaults on the iPhone, with 384,865 US ratings in October 2026. It's also built around an account: you sign in with an email address, and backups go to Keepsafe's own cloud. If you'd rather not tie private photos to an email account and a company's servers, here are the alternatives and how they differ.
Only deciding between Vaultaire and Keepsafe? See Vaultaire vs Keepsafe , compared point by point.
### Why do people look for Keepsafe alternatives?
Usually because of the account, the cloud, or the price. These are the points Keepsafe's own pages and App Store listing describe:
- An email account. Keepsafe uses an account tied to your email; its help center has a page on what to do if you lose access to that email ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
- Keepsafe's own cloud. Premium's "Private Cloud" stores up to 10,000 items with Keepsafe, and "Space Saver" compresses photos on the phone and keeps originals in that cloud (App Store listing).
- Price. The US listing shows Keepsafe Premium from $4.99 up to $35.99, including $9.99 a month or $23.99 a year.
- Tracking. Keepsafe's App Store privacy label lists Usage Data as "Data Used to Track You".
None of that makes Keepsafe unsafe. Keepsafe's help center says it encrypts files with AES-256 ( source ). It's a different model: the company holds your account and your cloud copy.
### Keepsafe alternatives with no account, compared
Every app here says in its App Store listing that it needs no account, except Apple's Hidden album, which is built into iOS.
No-account alternatives to Keepsafe. Source: each app's US App Store page, 22 October 2026.

Vaultaire Pattern AES-256-GCM Your iCloud, encrypted, Free and Pro Yes None

### Is Vaultaire a good Keepsafe alternative?
Yes, if the account is what you want to leave behind. Vaultaire needs no account and backs up, encrypted, to your own iCloud, including on its free plan. Keepsafe signs you in with an email address and keeps its cloud copy on its own servers. Our Vaultaire review and Keepsafe review look at each app on its own.

Price, encryption, backup and decoy vaults side by side: Vaultaire vs Keepsafe compared .
### Which Keepsafe alternative should you choose?
Pick by what mattered to you about leaving Keepsafe.
- No account, encrypted iCloud backup, and a decoy: Noxium or Vaultaire. Both open with a drawn pattern and include encrypted iCloud backup on the free plan. Noxium's free plan holds 150 photos and 10 videos; Vaultaire's holds 100 photos and 10 videos.
- Open-source encryption you can read: Obscura or Encamera. Obscura keeps everything on the device and says there is no recovery if you forget your password.
- Nothing to install: Apple's Hidden album. It's free and locked with Face ID, but anyone with your passcode can open it. See is the Hidden album private?
Whatever you pick, check one thing before you move years of photos: what happens if you forget your code. With no account, there's no email reset. Noxium has you write down a recovery phrase at setup for exactly this.
### How do you switch from Keepsafe without losing photos?
Export from Keepsafe back to Photos, check everything arrived at full quality, move it into the new vault, and only then delete Keepsafe's copies.
- If you used Space Saver, the full-size originals live in Keepsafe's cloud, not on the phone. Make sure you export the originals, not the compressed copies: open a few photos and check they're full quality before you go on.
- Export from Keepsafe to your Photos library, album by album. Note how many items each album has.
- Check the export in Photos: counts match, videos play, Live Photos move.
- Import into the new vault, and let it delete the originals from Photos if it offers to. Then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
- Check the new vault's backup has finished.
- Only then delete items from Keepsafe and cancel the subscription in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Exported photos sit unencrypted in your Photos library until the new vault imports them. Do the move in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.
Noxium has no sign-up and no account. The backup goes to your own iCloud.
No account. No email. No ads.

Does Keepsafe need an account?
Yes. Keepsafe uses an account tied to your email address, and its cloud backup is stored with Keepsafe.
What is the best Keepsafe alternative without an account?
It depends on what you need. For encrypted iCloud backup and a decoy vault, Noxium and Vaultaire both work without an account. For open-source encryption, look at Obscura or Encamera.
Can I move my photos from Keepsafe to another vault?
Yes. Export them from Keepsafe to Photos, check they arrived at full quality, import them into the new vault, and only then delete them from Keepsafe.
If a vault has no account, how do I recover it if I forget my code?
Only through whatever recovery the app gives you, such as a recovery phrase you keep yourself. With no account, there is no email reset, so set up recovery before you need it.

# Vaultaire vs Keepsafe: which photo vault fits you?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/vaultaire-vs-keepsafe
Last updated: 2026-11-12

Guide · Comparison
## Vaultaire vs Keepsafe: which photo vault fits you?
By Inertia Projects · Published 26 October 2026 · Last updated 12 November 2026
Short answer
The main difference is who holds your photos. Vaultaire needs no account and backs up, encrypted, to your own iCloud, including on its free plan. Keepsafe signs you in with an email address and keeps its cloud copy on Keepsafe's own servers. From their US App Store listings in October 2026, Vaultaire sells a $39.99 lifetime plan and lists no data used to track you; Keepsafe is subscription-based and lists Usage Data as used to track you.
Keepsafe is one of the best-known photo vaults on the iPhone, with 384,865 US ratings in October 2026. Vaultaire is new, with 46. Both hide photos and videos behind a lock, but they're built on different ideas about accounts and the cloud. This guide compares them point by point, using each app's App Store listing and its own published pages, so you can pick the one that fits how you want your photos stored.
### How do Vaultaire and Keepsafe differ?
Vaultaire works without an account and keeps backups in your iCloud; Keepsafe works through an email account and its own cloud. The rest of the differences follow from that.
Vaultaire and Keepsafe side by side. Source: each app's US App Store page, 21–22 October 2026, and the Keepsafe Help Center.

### Do you need an account for Vaultaire or Keepsafe?
Vaultaire doesn't ask for one. Keepsafe does: you sign in with an email address.
An account gives you an email address to recover through. The cost is that your vault is tied to that address and to a company's records. Keepsafe's help center has a page on what to do if you lose access to that email ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
With no account, nobody can reset your code for you. Before you trust a no-account vault with years of photos, check what it offers if you forget your code. Our guide on forgotten vault passwords covers what to look for.
### Where do Vaultaire and Keepsafe back up your photos?
Vaultaire backs up to your own iCloud, encrypted, on both its free and Pro plans. Keepsafe backs up to its own cloud, called Private Cloud.
- Vaultaire: the listing says backups are encrypted and go to your iCloud, on the free plan too.
- Keepsafe: the free plan backs up your first 200 items ( Keepsafe Help Center ). Premium raises Private Cloud to 10,000 items, and its "Space Saver" keeps small copies on the phone and the originals in Keepsafe's cloud.
Watch out
If you use Keepsafe's Space Saver, the full-size originals are in Keepsafe's cloud, not on your phone. If you ever leave Keepsafe, export the originals, not the small copies.
### Which is cheaper, Vaultaire or Keepsafe?
For long-term use, Vaultaire: it sells a $39.99 lifetime plan, while Keepsafe's listing shows only Premium subscriptions and plans.
Keepsafe's US listing shows $9.99 a month or $23.99 a year, with purchases from $4.99 to $35.99. Vaultaire's listing shows weekly, monthly and annual Pro subscriptions alongside the $39.99 lifetime purchase, with purchases from $1.99 to $99.99. Prices differ by country and change; check the App Store in your region before you buy. More apps with one-time prices are in vaults without subscriptions or ads .
### Which one is more secure?
Both say they encrypt your files. Vaultaire names the method in its listing (AES-256-GCM); Keepsafe's listing says "military-grade", and its help center says AES-256 ( source ).
The bigger difference is where copies live. With Vaultaire, the only copies are on your devices and in your iCloud. With Keepsafe, a copy also lives on Keepsafe's servers, tied to your account. For what the encryption terms mean, see how encrypted photo vaults work .
### Does Vaultaire or Keepsafe have a decoy vault?
Vaultaire does: a different pattern opens a different vault, and Pro adds a duress vault. Keepsafe's App Store listing doesn't mention a decoy.
A decoy vault opens a harmless set of photos if someone makes you unlock the app. It only helps if the decoy looks real. Our guide on what a decoy vault is explains how they work and their limits.
### Should you choose Vaultaire or Keepsafe?
Choose Vaultaire if you don't want an account or a company cloud. Choose Keepsafe if you want an email account to fall back on and don't mind its cloud.
- Vaultaire fits if you want no account, an encrypted backup in your own iCloud, a decoy vault, and a one-time price.
- Keepsafe fits if you want an email account you can recover through, and you're comfortable with Keepsafe storing your cloud copy and with its subscription prices.
Moving from Keepsafe? Follow the steps in how to switch from Keepsafe without losing photos : export the originals, check them, import, and only then delete.

Yes. Noxium photo vault, which we make, works the same way as Vaultaire on the points above: no account, a drawn pattern, AES-256-GCM, and an encrypted backup to your own iCloud on the free plan.
The differences: Noxium's free plan holds 150 photos and 10 videos with 1 decoy vault, you write down a recovery phrase at setup in case you forget your pattern, and its privacy label is Data Not Collected. Pro is $2.99 a week, $17.99 a year or $39.99 once. For the full side-by-side, read our Vaultaire review, compared with Noxium .

# How to lock photos on iPhone with Face ID, a passcode or a pattern

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/lock-photos-iphone-face-id
Last updated: 2026-11-18

Guide · Locking photos
## How to lock photos on iPhone with Face ID, a passcode or a pattern
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 18 November 2026
Short answer
iPhone can lock photos with Face ID in three built-in ways: hide them so they go into the Hidden album (locked by default), make the whole Photos app require Face ID, or put them in a locked note. All three fall back to your iPhone passcode. For a lock that's separate from your passcode, such as a pattern, you need a photo vault app.
There's no "lock this album" button in the Photos app. Instead, iOS 26 gives you a few locks that work at different levels: one album, the whole app, or a single note. Here's how to set up each one, what it actually locks, and when you need something stronger.
### How do you lock photos in the Hidden album with Face ID?
Hide the photos, then make sure the Hidden album's Face ID lock is on. It's on by default since iOS 16. For how that compares with a separate vault, see Hidden album vs a photo vault app .
- Hide the photos: in Photos, touch and hold a photo and tap Hide . For several, tap Select , choose them, tap More (…) and Hide .
- Check the lock: go to Settings › Apps › Photos and turn on Use Face ID (or Use Touch ID / Use Passcode). This locks both Hidden and Recently Deleted.
- Optional: turn off Show Hidden Album so the album doesn't appear in Collections at all.
Where the Hidden album is, how to view and unhide photos, and what happens to them on iCloud and a new iPhone: hidden photos on iPhone, the complete guide .
Photos can't lock other albums. Only Hidden and Recently Deleted have a lock. And the lock accepts your iPhone passcode, so anyone who knows it can open the album ( Apple Support ).
### How do you lock hidden photos on iPhone?
Turn on Use Face ID in Settings › Apps › Photos . Once it's on, the Hidden album asks for Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode every time it opens.
- Open Settings › Apps › Photos .
- Turn on Use Face ID (Use Touch ID or Use Passcode on iPhones without Face ID).
- Test it: in Photos, open Collections › Utilities › Hidden . It should ask for Face ID before showing anything.
- Hide the album itself, if you like, by turning off Show Hidden Album in the same settings.
If the album opens without asking, the switch is off. Hidden photos still sync to every device on your Apple Account with iCloud Photos, and each one has its own Face ID setting.
### What's the difference between hiding and locking photos?
Hiding moves a photo out of your main library; locking puts something in front of it. The Hidden album does both, but its lock is your iPhone's own Face ID and passcode.
- Hidden only: with the Face ID switch off, anyone holding your unlocked phone can open the Hidden album.
- Hidden and locked: someone needs your face or your iPhone passcode.
- Locked with a separate code: a locked note with its own Notes password, or a vault app with its own pattern or PIN, stays shut even for someone who knows your passcode.
- Encrypted with a separate key: in an encrypted vault app, the key comes from your vault code, so the files are unreadable without it. See how encrypted photo vaults work .
### Can you lock one album on iPhone?
Not in Photos. iOS locks only Hidden and Recently Deleted. To lock an album of your choice, use a vault app with per-album locks; in Noxium Pro, any album can have its own pattern , and the album stays locked inside the open vault until that pattern is drawn.
### How do you lock the whole Photos app?
Since iOS 18, you can make any app ask for Face ID before it opens.
- Touch and hold the Photos icon on the Home Screen.
- Tap Require Face ID and confirm.
Now Photos asks for Face ID every time it opens, which stops someone you've handed your unlocked phone from browsing your library. It's all or nothing, though: you'll unlock your whole library many times a day, and the passcode still opens it.
### How do you lock photos in a note?
Add photos to a note, then lock the note. Notes can use a separate password from your iPhone passcode, with Face ID as a shortcut. (For notes that open only with a vault pattern, see encrypted notes in Noxium , which we make.)
- In Notes , create a note, tap the camera button and choose Choose Photo or Video .
- Tap More (…) and Lock .
- To use a separate password, go to Settings › Apps › Notes › Password , choose a Notes password, and turn on Use Face ID .
- Delete the originals from Photos, then from Recently Deleted.
This is the only built-in lock that can be separate from your passcode. It suits a handful of photos, not a library: there are no albums, and long videos are awkward. If you forget a separate Notes password, Apple can't recover the locked notes.
### How do you show someone one photo without them swiping?
Use Guided Access. It locks the iPhone to the app you're in, so the other person can't leave it.
- Turn it on once in Settings › Accessibility › Guided Access , and set a passcode.
- Open the photo, then triple-click the side button and tap Start . You can circle areas of the screen to disable them.
- To end it, triple-click the side button and enter the Guided Access passcode.
Guided Access doesn't stop swiping between photos inside Photos unless you disable touch on the screen, so circle the whole photo or turn off Touch in its options.
### Can you lock photos with a pattern on iPhone?
Not with built-in features. iOS uses Face ID, Touch ID and passcodes; a drawn pattern lock comes only from vault apps. Private Photo Vault, Vaultaire and Noxium, among others, offer a pattern according to their App Store listings and websites.
A pattern is only as good as what's behind it. In some apps it just opens a screen in front of normal files; in others it's used to derive the encryption key. Ask how the app uses it before you trust it (we explain the difference in how encrypted photo vaults work ).
In Noxium, which we make, you draw a pattern across at least 6 of the 25 bolts on a 5×5 plate. The pattern is never stored: it's stretched with Argon2id into the key that opens your vault, and every photo is encrypted on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM. Face ID can open the main vault for convenience, but never a decoy vault.
Noxium's lock: a pattern across a 5×5 plate of bolts, separate from your iPhone passcode.
Get Noxium free on the App Store →

### Questions people ask
Can someone open my Hidden album without Face ID?
Yes, if they know your iPhone passcode: the lock falls back to it. If Use Face ID is off in Photos settings, it doesn't ask at all.
Does hiding a photo encrypt it?
No more than any other photo. iPhone encrypts its storage as a whole, and hiding only moves the photo to a locked album; it doesn't add a separate key.
Can I lock a specific album on iPhone?
No. The Photos app only locks the Hidden and Recently Deleted albums. To lock other photos, hide them, put them in a locked note, or use a vault app.
Can I lock photos with a different password than my iPhone passcode?
Yes, in two ways: a locked note with a separate Notes password, or a vault app with its own PIN, password or pattern.
Does locking the Photos app hide it?
No. Require Face ID only asks for Face ID when Photos opens. The app stays on your Home Screen.
Is a pattern lock safer than a PIN?
Not automatically. What matters is whether the code is used to encrypt the photos and how slow it is to guess. A long pattern or password used to derive an encryption key is far stronger than a 4-digit PIN in front of normal files.

# What is a decoy vault, and does it actually protect you?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/what-is-a-decoy-vault
Last updated: 2026-11-19

Guide · Decoy vaults
## What is a decoy vault, and does it actually protect you?
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 19 November 2026
Short answer
A decoy vault is a second, harmless vault inside a photo vault app that opens when you enter a different PIN, password or pattern. If someone pressures you to open the app, you open the decoy, and they see ordinary photos instead of your private ones. It helps in a tense moment, but it isn't a guarantee: it works best when nothing in the app reveals that a second vault exists.
Picture someone who knows you use a vault app (a partner, a parent, someone at a border) saying "open it". Refusing makes things worse. A decoy vault gives you a third option: open it, and show them something harmless. Here's how decoy vaults work, the two very different ways apps build them, and their honest limits.
### How does a decoy vault work?
The app accepts more than one code. Your real code opens your real vault. A second code opens a separate vault you've filled with ordinary photos. To anyone watching, both look like you simply opened the app.
You'll also see it called a fake PIN, decoy password, fake vault or secondary passcode. The idea is the same; how well it's built varies a lot.
### What are the two kinds of decoy vault?
Some apps show a fake screen; others open a genuinely separate, encrypted vault.
- A fake screen or fake gallery. The decoy code opens a different view in the same app, often with a settings menu that still shows the decoy option. Anyone who looks through the app's settings, or knows the app, may see that a decoy exists.
- A separate encrypted vault. Each code unlocks its own vault with its own encryption key. The app can't show a list of vaults, because it can't read the other vaults without their codes. A wrong code simply opens nothing.
The second kind is much harder to see through, because nothing inside the decoy points to anything else.
### What can't a decoy vault do?
A decoy buys you a calm moment; it doesn't make your real photos disappear.
- It has to be believable. An empty decoy, or one with three photos, invites more questions. Put real, boring photos in it and add a few now and then.
- It doesn't beat a determined expert. Storage usage, backups, or forensic tools may show there's more data than the decoy explains.
- Face ID can give it away in apps where Face ID opens your real vault while someone watches. Use the decoy code when you're under pressure, not Face ID.
- It's not legal protection. Laws on unlocking devices differ by country. A decoy is a privacy tool, not advice on what you must or mustn't do.
### How is a decoy vault different from an emergency erase or duress code?
A decoy hides your vault; an emergency erase code destroys it. Some apps offer a third code that opens a harmless vault and, at the same time, quietly deletes the others. That protects the photos from being seen, but they're gone. If the app can also delete the cloud backup, there's no way back.
Only set up an erase code if losing those photos is better than them being seen, and keep a copy elsewhere if you can't afford to lose them.
### Which photo vault apps have a decoy vault?
From their App Store listings, checked 22 October to 15 November 2026. App names link to our full reviews where we have one.
Decoy features named in each app's US App Store description, checked 22 October to 15 November 2026
App What the listing says
Noxium Our app A second pattern opens a separate encrypted vault; 1 free, more with Pro. Emergency erase pattern with Pro.
Vaultaire A different pattern opens a different vault; duress vault with Pro.
Private Photo Vault Decoy password.
Secret Photo Album (SA) Decoy PIN.
PV – Secret Photo Album Fake password.
Safe Lock Fake password that opens a fake gallery.
KYMS Fake PIN for a decoy vault.
Privault A secondary passcode opens a secondary folder.
Secret Photo Vault – Lock Photos Decoy accounts with their own passwords.
Hide it Pro No decoy; an escape code makes the app look empty.
Calculator# No decoy; a panic switch jumps to another app.
Apple Hidden album No decoy.
Listings don't say which kind of decoy they are, so test it: open the decoy and look through every screen, including settings. If anything mentions another vault, so will the person looking. See all 17 apps in our comparison .
### How do you test a decoy before you need it?
Open it as if you were the other person, and look for anything that gives the real vault away. Five minutes now saves a bad moment later.
- Open the decoy with its own code, from a locked app.
- Go through every screen , settings included. Anything that names another vault, counts more items than you can see, or offers to "switch vault" is a giveaway.
- Check the backup or storage screens. A total that's far larger than the decoy's contents invites questions.
- Try Face ID. If it opens the real vault, leave Face ID off or practise using the decoy code under pressure.
- Add a few new photos now and then, so the decoy's latest items aren't months old.
### How do you set up a decoy vault well?
- Pick a code you won't mix up with your real one, but can recall under stress.
- Fill it with real, dull photos: food, a trip, screenshots, a pet. Dozens, not three.
- Use it now and then so the dates aren't all from one day.
- Practise opening it once or twice so you don't hesitate when it matters.
- Check nothing gives it away: open the decoy and look through settings, albums and counts.
In Noxium, which we make, each pattern derives its own key, so a decoy is a separate encrypted vault. Noxium never shows a list of vaults, nothing in the decoy marks it as a decoy, and Face ID only ever opens your main vault. You add one in Settings with "Add a decoy vault" and draw its pattern. The free plan includes one.
In Noxium, a second pattern opens a decoy vault that looks like an ordinary Noxium.
A second pattern, a harmless vault
Noxium's decoy vault is a separate encrypted vault with its own pattern, included free. Face ID never opens it, and nothing in it points to your real one. See how Noxium's decoy vault works , and Pro's emergency erase pattern .

### Questions people ask
Can you have more than one decoy vault?
In some apps. Noxium's free plan includes 1 decoy vault and Pro adds as many as you like; other apps' listings usually describe a single decoy code.
What is a fake PIN in a photo vault app?
A second PIN that opens a different, harmless set of photos instead of your private ones. It's another name for a decoy vault.
Can someone tell I'm using a decoy vault?
Possibly. Apps that show the decoy option in settings, or decoys with very few photos, are easy to spot. A decoy that's a separate encrypted vault, filled with ordinary photos, is much harder to see through.
Does the Hidden album have a decoy?
No. The Hidden album opens with Face ID or your iPhone passcode, and there's no second, harmless version.
Is a decoy vault the same as a duress code?
No. A decoy only opens a harmless vault. A duress or emergency erase code also deletes your other vaults, which can't be undone.

# How to hide videos on iPhone, and keep them playable

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/how-to-hide-videos-on-iphone
Last updated: 2026-11-18

Guide · Hiding videos
## How to hide videos on iPhone, and keep them playable
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 18 November 2026
Short answer
To hide a video on iPhone, touch and hold it in Photos and tap Hide. It moves to the Hidden album, which is locked with Face ID. For videos that must stay private even from someone who knows your passcode, use a vault app with its own code, and check that it keeps videos at full quality and plays large ones without trouble.
Hiding a video works the same way as hiding a photo, but videos bring their own problems: they're big, they fill iCloud, and they're where vault apps most often let people down. In the most recent one- and two-star reviews of eight popular vault apps, which we read in October 2026, video problems came up 40 times. Here's how to hide videos and keep them playable.
### How do you hide a video in the Photos app?
The same way as a photo: touch and hold, then Hide.
- Open Photos and find the video. Collections › Media Types › Videos lists them all.
- Touch and hold it , tap Hide , and confirm. For several, tap Select , choose them, tap More (…) and Hide .
- Check the lock: in Settings › Apps › Photos , make sure Use Face ID is on.
The video moves to Collections › Utilities › Hidden , keeps its full quality, and plays as normal. As with photos, your iPhone passcode opens the Hidden album, and hidden videos sync to your other devices with iCloud Photos. More on that in is the Hidden album private?
### How do you find hidden videos later?
Open Collections › Utilities › Hidden in Photos and unlock it with Face ID. Hidden videos don't show in Media Types › Videos or anywhere else in your library.
- Open Photos and scroll to Utilities in Collections.
- Tap Hidden and unlock it with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode.
- Can't see it? Turn on Settings › Apps › Photos › Show Hidden Album .
- To unhide a video, touch and hold it and tap Unhide .
For everything else about the album, including what happens on a new iPhone, see hidden photos on iPhone .
### Can you hide a video in a locked note?
Yes, but it's only practical for short clips. Add the video to a note with the camera button, then lock the note with More (…) › Lock . Large videos make notes slow to open and sync, and there's no gallery to browse.
### How do you hide videos in a vault app?
Import them from Photos into the vault, check they play, then delete the originals from Photos and Recently Deleted. Our import and export page walks through doing that without leaving copies. Before you trust a vault with videos, check four things:
- Does it keep full quality? Some vaults compress videos, or keep originals only in their own cloud. Look for "original quality" or similar in the listing.
- Does it handle big files? 4K, HDR, slow-motion and long videos are often several gigabytes. Import one long video as a test.
- Do videos play without waiting? Some encrypted vaults decrypt the whole file before playing it, which takes time and space. Better ones decrypt as they play.
- Are videos in the free plan? Many free plans limit videos more than photos. Noxium's free plan, for example, holds 10 videos.
In Noxium, which we make, videos are encrypted on the iPhone in 1 MiB chunks with AES-256-GCM. Because each chunk can be decrypted on its own, even long 4K videos start playing straight away, without a decrypted copy written to storage. Videos keep their original quality and date, and export back to Photos the same way. You can also record videos straight into the vault with its camera, so they never touch your camera roll.
Photos and videos in a Noxium vault, encrypted on the iPhone.
Get Noxium free on the App Store →
### Why do videos cause trouble in vault apps?
Size, mostly. A minute of 4K video can be hundreds of megabytes, so anything a vault does to a video (import, encrypt, back up, restore) takes longer and fails more often than with photos.
- Import fails or stops when the app is closed mid-way or the phone runs low on space.
- Backups lag behind, especially if they only run on Wi-Fi or iCloud is nearly full, so the newest videos are the ones missing after a restore.
- Playback stalls when the app decrypts the whole file first.
- Formats get lost: Live Photos can lose their video part, and HDR can be flattened, if the app re-encodes.
After importing, play a few videos from the start, middle and end, and check one Live Photo still moves.
### What happens to hidden videos in backups?
They're backed up like any other video. Hiding doesn't take a video out of iCloud Photos or an iCloud Backup.
- With iCloud Photos on, hidden videos sync to your other devices and stay in the Hidden album there.
- With iCloud Photos off, your photos and videos are part of your iPhone's iCloud Backup instead.
- In a vault app, it depends on the app: some keep videos only on the phone, some upload to their own cloud, and some back up to your iCloud. Noxium uploads only encrypted data to your private iCloud; see encrypted iCloud backup .
### How much storage do hidden videos take?
The same as before you hid them, and sometimes double for a while. Hiding in Photos doesn't change size. Moving videos into a vault creates a second copy until you delete the originals, so make sure you have free space for the largest videos first.
If the vault backs up to iCloud, videos count toward your iCloud storage too. Check Settings › [your name] › iCloud before a big import. In Noxium you can keep videos from using mobile data with Wi-Fi only for videos in the backup settings.
### What should you clean up after hiding videos?
- Recently Deleted: deleted originals stay for 30 days. Open Collections › Utilities › Recently Deleted , unlock it, and delete them for good.
- Messages and chat apps: a video you sent or received has its own copy in that conversation.
- Shared albums and the Shared Library: people you shared with can still see it.
- Your computer: check old imports on a Mac or PC.
Big videos, played straight away
Noxium encrypts videos on your iPhone in small chunks, so even long 4K videos play without waiting, at full quality. Free for 10 videos and 150 photos.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Can someone see my hidden videos if they know my passcode?
Yes. The Hidden album's lock accepts your iPhone passcode. To keep videos private from someone who knows it, use a vault app with its own code.
Can you hide videos on iPhone without an app?
Yes. Touch and hold the video in Photos and tap Hide. It moves to the Hidden album, which opens with Face ID or your passcode.
Do hidden videos lose quality?
Not in the Photos app; hiding doesn't change the file. Some vault apps compress videos or keep the original only in their cloud, so check before you move large videos into one.
Why won't my videos play in my vault app?
Usually because the full-size video is still downloading from the app's cloud, the import didn't finish, or the app has to decrypt the whole file first. Keep the app open on Wi-Fi, and contact the developer if one video never plays.
Do hidden videos still use iCloud storage?
Yes. Hidden videos in Photos count toward iCloud Photos, and videos in a vault that backs up to iCloud count toward your iCloud storage.

# Photo vault apps without a subscription or ads

Guide · Pricing
## Photo vault apps without a subscription or ads
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 21 November 2026
Short answer
Several iPhone photo vaults sell a one-time purchase instead of, or alongside, a subscription: on the US App Store in October 2026 these include Vaultaire ($39.99 lifetime), Obscura ($39.99), Noxium ($39.99, which we make), Privault ($45.99) and PV ($41.99). Ads are a separate question: Calculator#, Privault, KYMS and PV say their free versions have ads or sell ad removal. The free options with no purchase at all are Apple's Hidden album and locked notes.
Pricing is the most common complaint in vault app reviews. In the most recent one- and two-star reviews of eight popular vault apps, which we read in October 2026, subscriptions and paywalls came up 67 times, more than lost photos. Here's which vaults let you pay once, which show ads, and the question that matters most: what happens to your photos if you stop paying.
### Why does a vault's pricing matter more than most apps'?
Because the app holds your photos. If a music app's subscription lapses, you lose music you can stream elsewhere. If a vault limits access when you stop paying, your own photos are on the other side of the paywall. Check the "if I stop paying" rule before you move a library in.
### Which photo vaults have a one-time purchase?
These apps list an in-app purchase named lifetime, permanent or similar on their US App Store page, rechecked 11–16 November 2026. Names are the developers'; we haven't bought them.

If you'll keep the app for more than about two years, usually yes. Divide the one-time price by the yearly price to see when it pays for itself.

### Which photo vault apps show ads?

- Calculator# says it is "free with ads".

Ads matter more than annoyance here: ad networks are a common reason an app's privacy label lists "Data Used to Track You". In our comparison, 9 of 17 vault apps reported tracking data.
### What do free plans include?
Free plans differ in what they cap. From each app's listing or help pages:
- Noxium: 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, and encrypted iCloud backup and restore.
- Vaultaire: up to 3 vaults, 100 photos and 10 videos in total, with encrypted iCloud backup.
- Keepsafe: the free plan covers your first 200 items ( Keepsafe Help Center ).
- Apple's Hidden album and locked notes: free and unlimited, apart from your iCloud storage.
Check whether backup is in the free plan. Some vaults charge for cloud backup, which means a free user's photos exist only on one phone.
### What happens to your photos if you stop paying?
Read this before anything else. The good answer is: you keep full access to everything already in the vault, including export and backup, and only new imports or premium features stop. The bad answer is anything that limits viewing, exporting or restoring your existing photos.
Noxium's rule, which we make: if Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault. Only adding past the free limits and Pro features (unlimited items, emergency erase, iPhone and iPad sync, custom icons, album patterns, shared vaults) pause.
Noxium: no ads, no account, and your photos stay yours if Pro ends.

### How do you choose a vault you won't regret paying for?
- Start free with a few dozen photos and a couple of videos. Test import, playback, export and backup.
- Find the "stop paying" rule in the app or its support pages.
- Compare a year of subscription with the one-time price. If you'll use it for years, one-time usually wins.
- Check the privacy label for "Data Used to Track You".
- Check Family Sharing if others in your household want it.

# Forgot your photo vault password or PIN? What you can still do

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/forgot-photo-vault-password
Last updated: 2026-11-19

Guide · Locked out
## Forgot your photo vault password or PIN? What you can still do
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 19 November 2026
Short answer
First, don't delete or reinstall the app; that can erase the vault for good. Then find out how your app handles recovery: some reset by email, some use a recovery phrase or key you saved at setup, and some truly encrypted vaults can't be opened by anyone without the code. Look in the app's lock screen and settings, check your email and notes for a recovery code, and contact the developer.
Getting locked out of a vault app is one of the most common complaints in vault reviews: in the most recent one- and two-star reviews of eight popular vault apps, which we read in October 2026, it came up 27 times. What you can do depends almost entirely on how the app was built, so this guide starts with what's safe to try, then explains each kind of recovery.
### What should you not do when you forget a vault code?
- Don't delete or reinstall the app. The vault lives in the app's storage. Deleting the app deletes it.
- Don't guess wildly. Many vaults add delays after wrong tries, and some can wipe after too many. Try a few likely codes, then stop.
- Don't pay an unlock service. If the vault is properly encrypted, no outside tool can open it. If it isn't, the developer can help you directly.
- Don't restore an old iPhone backup over your phone hoping for an older code. You could lose newer photos and data.
### What should you try first?
- Look for a "Forgot" option on the app's lock screen: forgot PIN, forgot password, use recovery phrase, or similar.
- Search your email for messages from the app: a recovery email, a setup confirmation, or a recovery code.
- Check where you keep passwords: Apple's Passwords app, a password manager, notes, or a paper note from when you set it up.
- Check other devices. If the vault is also on your iPad, it might still be unlocked there or use Face ID.
- Try Face ID or Touch ID if you turned it on. It may still open the vault even if you've forgotten the code.
- Contact the developer (App Store page › App Support). Give your app version and iPhone model. Never send them other passwords.
### How does vault recovery work?
There are three models, and each trades convenience against privacy.
The three ways vault apps handle a forgotten code
Recovery model How you get back in The trade-off
Email or account reset The developer emails you a reset or code Easy to recover, but someone with your email, or the developer, can too
Recovery phrase or key you keep Enter the phrase or key you saved at setup Nobody else can reset it, so losing both the code and the phrase locks you out
No recovery Only the code opens it Maximum privacy, no second chance
An app that can reset your code by email holds, or can rebuild, the key to your vault. That's not automatically bad, but it means your photos are only as private as your email account.
### How do popular vault apps handle a forgotten code?
From each developer's own App Store listing or help pages, checked October and November 2026. Full reviews are linked where we've written one.
- PV – Secret Photo Album: set a recovery email in the app's settings; it's used if you forget the passcode.
- Keepsafe: account-based, tied to your email. Its help center covers losing access to that email ( Keepsafe Help Center ). More in our Keepsafe review .
- Hide it Pro: lists a "Password Reset" in-app purchase for $4.99. See our Hide it Pro review .
- Calculator#: recovery through an email you register in the app. It's a safety net, but anyone with access to that email may be able to use it too. See our Calculator# review .
- Private Photo Vault: the listing doesn't describe recovery for the app lock. It warns that a forgotten Cloud Vault Password means losing access to your Cloud Vault data. See our Private Photo Vault review .
- Privault: the listing doesn't say what happens if you forget the passcode. Contact the developer before you need it; see our Privault review .
- Secret Photo Vault – Lock Photos: an optional security question can reset the password, if you set one up. See our Secret Photo Vault review .
- Vaultaire: a recovery sentence you save at setup, which can be viewed again later from the open vault's settings. See our Vaultaire review .
- Obscura: says plainly that if you forget your password, your photos are gone, with no reset or recovery email.
- Noxium (which we make): no reset by anyone, including us or Apple. At setup you write down a recovery phrase ; on the lock screen, tap "Forgot your pattern?", enter the phrase, and it opens your main vault.
Noxium asks you to write down a recovery phrase at setup. It's the only spare key.

### What if you forgot your iPhone passcode (Hidden album)?
Apple's Hidden album opens with Face ID or your iPhone passcode. If Face ID still works, it still opens. If you changed your passcode in the last 72 hours, iOS 17 and later let you use the previous one from the lock screen's "Forgot Passcode?" option.
Otherwise, the only way back is to erase the iPhone with a computer or in Recovery Mode, then restore from a backup ( Apple: reset your iPhone and passcode ). Photos in iCloud Photos come back when you sign in again; anything that was only on the phone and not in a backup is lost.
### Which recovery method is safest?
The one only you can use. Each kind of recovery trades convenience against who else could get in.
Ways vault apps let you back in after a forgotten code
Method Who else could use it Example from the list above
Email reset Anyone with access to that email account Calculator#, PV, Keepsafe
Security question Anyone who knows or can guess the answer Secret Photo Vault – Lock Photos
Paid reset Depends on how the developer verifies you Hide it Pro
Recovery phrase you keep Only someone who finds your written phrase Noxium, Vaultaire
No recovery Nobody, including you Obscura
If the developer can reset your code, the developer, or someone who gets into your email, can in principle get in too. A recovery phrase avoids that, but only if you write it down and keep it somewhere safe. For how a phrase opens an encrypted vault, see how encrypted photo vaults work .
### How do you avoid getting locked out next time?
- Save the code in Apple's Passwords app or a password manager, with a note of which app it's for.
- Set up recovery now, whatever your app offers, and test it once.
- Write a recovery phrase on paper and keep it somewhere safe, away from the phone.
- Keep a backup you understand, so a lockout isn't also a loss. See how to recover photos a vault app lost .

### Questions people ask
Is a security question a safe way to recover a vault?
It's the weakest option. Answers such as a pet's name or a first school are often easy to guess or find. If your app offers one, use an answer nobody could know.
Can a photo vault app reset my password?
Only if it was built that way, usually through your email or an account. Vaults that encrypt with a key only you hold can't reset it; they rely on a recovery phrase or key you saved.
Can I recover a vault if I deleted the app?
Only from a backup: the app's cloud, your iCloud, or a computer copy. Deleting the app deletes the vault stored on the phone.
Is there software that can unlock a photo vault?
Not for a properly encrypted vault. Treat any paid unlock tool or service as a scam, and contact the app's developer instead.

Tap "Forgot your pattern?" on the lock screen and enter the phrase you wrote down at setup. If you've lost both, nobody can open the vault, including us.

# How encrypted photo vaults work, in plain English

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/how-encrypted-photo-vaults-work
Last updated: 2026-11-22

Guide · Encryption explained
## How encrypted photo vaults work, in plain English
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 22 November 2026
Short answer
An encrypted photo vault scrambles each photo with a secret key, so the file is unreadable without it. Your PIN, password or pattern is turned into that key (or into a key that unlocks it) on your phone, slowly on purpose, so guessing is expensive. A vault that only shows a PIN screen in front of normal files is hiding photos, not encrypting them.
Vault apps love the word "encrypted", and some add "military-grade". Neither tells you much. This guide explains, without math, what real encryption in a photo vault involves, so you can read an app's claims and know what they mean.
### What's the difference between hiding and encrypting a photo?
Hiding puts a door in front of a normal photo. Encrypting turns the photo itself into unreadable data.
A vault that only hides stores your photos as ordinary image files inside the app, and shows a PIN screen before it displays them. Anyone who gets at those files another way (a computer backup, a forensic tool, a bug) sees the photos. An encrypting vault stores only scrambled data. Without the key, even a perfect copy of the files is useless.
### What is an encryption key?
A key is a long random number that the encryption uses to scramble and unscramble data. A 256-bit key has about 10 77 possible values, far beyond what any computer could try, so nobody guesses the key itself.
That's why attackers don't go after the key. They go after the thing that unlocks it: your code.
### How does a PIN or pattern become a key?
Through a "key derivation function", which turns your code into a key. Good ones are deliberately slow and memory-hungry, so each guess costs real time.
This matters because codes are short. A 4-digit PIN has 10,000 possibilities. If each guess took a microsecond, a computer would try them all in a hundredth of a second. If each guess takes half a second and a lot of memory, the same search takes over an hour for a 4-digit PIN, and grows enormously with every extra character or bolt. A long random password becomes impractical to guess.
- Argon2id is the current recommended choice. It's "memory-hard", which makes it expensive to speed up with graphics cards or custom chips.
- PBKDF2 is older and still common. It's slow, but cheaper to attack with specialised hardware.
- A plain hash, or nothing, means guesses are nearly free.
Noxium, which we make, uses Argon2id with 64 MiB of memory and 3 passes, plus a random 128-bit salt so the same pattern never produces the same key twice. Our page on Noxium's pattern lock shows how many patterns the 5×5 plate allows.
### What does AES-256-GCM mean?
It's the cipher that scrambles the photos, in a mode that also detects tampering.
- AES is the standard cipher used by governments, banks and your iPhone itself.
- 256 is the key size in bits.
- GCM adds an authentication tag: if a single bit of the encrypted file is changed or damaged, decryption fails instead of producing a corrupted photo.
"Military-grade encryption" usually just means AES. The interesting questions are what the key comes from, where it's kept, and whether the backup is encrypted too.
### Why do good vaults use "keys inside keys"?
So you can change your code without re-encrypting every photo, and so one leaked file key doesn't expose the rest.
- Your code is stretched into a wrapping key .
- The wrapping key unlocks a random vault key , stored only in encrypted form.
- The vault key unlocks a separate random file key for every photo, video and note.
Changing your code only re-wraps the vault key. A recovery phrase works the same way: it's a second wrapping of the same vault key, so either the code or the phrase opens the vault. Large videos are often encrypted in chunks, so they can play without decrypting the whole file first. Noxium uses 1 MiB chunks, each with its own authentication tag. The full key hierarchy is on our security section , and every layer is explained on our on-device encryption page.
### How does an encrypted backup stay private?
By encrypting on the phone before anything is uploaded, so the cloud only ever stores scrambled data. This is called end-to-end encryption.
The test is simple: could the company reset your code by email and give you your photos back? If yes, they can reach the key, and so could anyone who gets into their systems or your email. If no, only you can decrypt the backup, which is also why losing both your code and your recovery phrase means losing access.
Noxium encrypts photos, thumbnails and their names, dates and places on the iPhone, then backs up only that ciphertext to your own private iCloud (CloudKit). Apple stores it but can't read it.
### What can encryption not protect against?
- Someone watching you enter your code, or making you enter it.
- An open vault. While it's unlocked on screen, the photos are visible. Good apps lock quickly and hide content in the app switcher, but none can block a screenshot: see photo vault screenshot protection .
- A short code. Slow key derivation helps, but a 4-digit PIN can still be tried exhaustively.
- Copies outside the vault, such as originals left in Photos, Messages or Recently Deleted.
### How can you tell if a vault really encrypts?
- It names the cipher and the key derivation (for example AES-256-GCM and Argon2id or PBKDF2), not just "secure".
- It says encryption happens on the device, before backup.
- It can't reset your code by email, or it says honestly that it can.
- Its backup is described as encrypted with your key, not just "secure cloud".
- Ideally, the encryption code is open source or independently reviewed.
In October 2026, only 2 of the 17 vault apps we compared named AES-256-GCM in their App Store description. See them all in our comparison .
### What do popular vault apps say about their encryption?
Few say much. Of the 15 vault apps we've reviewed, only Vaultaire and Obscura name their cipher in their listings. Keepsafe names AES-256 in its help center, and Obscura and Encamera publish their encryption code. The rest say "encrypted" without details, or don't mention encryption.
What each app's US App Store listing (and, where noted, its own help pages or code) says about encryption, checked 11 to 22 November 2026. We report claims, not test results.
App What it says about encryption
Vaultaire AES-256-GCM on the device; iCloud backup encrypted before upload
Obscura AES-256-GCM; key from your password through PBKDF2, 600,000 rounds; publishes its encryption code
Encamera Encrypts all media; publishes its encryption code, built on libsodium
Keepsafe "Military-grade" in the listing; AES-256 in its help center
KYMS "AES military-grade"; key size and mode not named
Privault Says storage is encrypted; cipher not named
Private Photo Vault Cloud backup called "encrypted"; cipher not named
PV - Secret Photo Album Mentions "data encryption"; cipher not named
HiddenVault "Zero-knowledge"; cipher not named
SPV - Secret Photo Vault Not mentioned; PIN protection
Secret Photo Vault Lock Photos Not mentioned
Safe Lock Not mentioned
MaxVault Not mentioned
Hide it Pro Not mentioned
Calculator# Not mentioned
Noxium (ours) AES-256-GCM on the device, key from your pattern through Argon2id; backup is ciphertext only
"Not mentioned" doesn't prove an app doesn't encrypt; it means you can't tell from what the developer publishes. If it matters to you, ask the developer the questions in the list above.
### Doesn't the iPhone already encrypt my photos?
Yes, while the phone is locked. Once it's unlocked, anyone holding it can open Photos, so a vault adds a second lock with its own key.
- On the iPhone. iOS encrypts its storage with keys tied to your passcode (Apple calls this Data Protection). That protects a lost, locked phone. It doesn't separate one app's photos from someone who knows or watches your passcode.
- The Hidden album. It needs Face ID or your passcode to open, but it's the same passcode, and it syncs to your other devices. See how to lock photos on iPhone .
- iCloud Photos. With Advanced Data Protection turned on, iCloud Photos is end-to-end encrypted. Without it, Apple holds the keys to your iCloud Photos.
A vault that encrypts with a key from its own code means your iPhone passcode alone doesn't open it.
### Does open-source code prove a vault is safe?
No, but it helps. Published code lets anyone check how files are encrypted, instead of trusting a word like "secure".
- It shows the method. You can see the cipher, how keys are made, and where they're stored.
- It isn't the same as an audit. Code being public doesn't mean someone qualified has reviewed it.
- It may not be the whole app. Some developers publish only the encryption part. That's the part that matters most, but the rest of the app still handles your photos.
- You can't easily confirm the App Store build matches. Apple doesn't let you check that the app you installed was built from the published code.
Noxium, which we make, isn't open source. We publish exactly what it uses instead: Argon2id, AES-256-GCM, the key layers and the chunk size, on our on-device encryption page.
In Noxium, your pattern is never stored. It's stretched with Argon2id into the key that opens your vault.
Encryption you can read about
Noxium names every piece: Argon2id for your pattern, AES-256-GCM for each file, and only ciphertext in your own iCloud. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Are photo vault apps encrypted?
Some are, some aren't. Many only show a PIN screen in front of ordinary files. Look for a named cipher, such as AES-256, and encryption on the device before backup.
What does military-grade encryption mean?
Usually just AES, the standard cipher. It doesn't tell you how the key is made or stored, which matters more.
What is Argon2id?
A key derivation function that turns a password or pattern into an encryption key slowly and with a lot of memory, so guessing codes is expensive.
Is Face ID part of the encryption?
Not directly. Face ID is a shortcut to a key the app stored in the iPhone's Keychain. In Noxium, that key stays on this iPhone, isn't synced, and stops working if your Face ID enrolment changes; your pattern always works.
Can an encrypted vault be hacked?
The encryption itself isn't the weak point. Short codes, codes seen by someone else, and unencrypted copies left elsewhere are. Use a long code and remove originals after importing.

# Are photo vault apps safe? What to check before you trust one

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/are-photo-vault-apps-safe
Last updated: 2026-10-26

Guide · Safety
## Are photo vault apps safe? What to check before you trust one
By Inertia Projects · Published 22 October 2026 · Last updated 26 October 2026
Short answer
Some are, and many aren't as safe as they sound. A safe vault encrypts photos on your phone with a key only you control, keeps a backup you can actually restore, and doesn't track you. Of 17 vault apps we checked in October 2026, 9 reported data used to track you, 6 didn't mention encryption in their App Store listing, and only 2 named AES-256-GCM.
"Is it safe?" can mean two things: will other people be unable to see my photos, and will I never lose them? A good vault has to do both, and the two pull against each other. Here are the real risks, what 17 apps' App Store pages show, and a checklist you can use on any vault.
### What are the real risks of photo vault apps?
- No real encryption. Some vaults only put a PIN screen in front of normal image files. Anyone who reaches the files another way can see them.
- Losing your photos. Vault photos are often left out of normal iPhone backups. A new phone, a reinstall or an expired subscription can leave them stranded. In recent one- and two-star reviews of eight popular vaults, lost or missing photos came up 47 times.
- Getting locked out. A forgotten code with no recovery option can mean losing everything.
- Your data going elsewhere. Ad and analytics SDKs, and backups on the developer's servers, mean your activity, or your photos, leave your control.
- Paywalls around your own photos. Some apps limit access when you stop paying.
### What do vault apps' App Store listings show?
We looked at 17 popular iPhone vault apps on 22 October 2026, using only what each developer says on its App Store page and the privacy label it reported to Apple:
17 iPhone photo vault apps, US App Store, 22 October 2026
Finding Apps
Report "Data Used to Track You" 9 of 17
Don't mention encryption in the listing 6 of 17
Name AES-256-GCM 2 of 17
Report "Data Not Collected" 3 of 17
Not mentioning encryption doesn't prove an app doesn't encrypt, and privacy labels are self-reported. But a vault that protects your photos well usually says how. App-by-app details are in our comparison .
### What should you check before trusting a photo vault?
- Encryption, named and on-device. Look for a specific cipher (AES-256) and a statement that photos are encrypted on the phone. "Secure" and "military-grade" alone tell you nothing. Our plain-English guide to how photo vault apps work explains what to look for.
- A backup you can restore. Where does it go, is it encrypted with your key, and how do you restore on a new iPhone? Is backup included in the free plan?
- Recovery that doesn't weaken privacy. A recovery phrase or key you keep is safer than an email reset the developer controls. No recovery at all is private but unforgiving.
- The privacy label. On the App Store page, check "Data Used to Track You". For a vault, the best answer is "Data Not Collected".
- The stop-paying rule. Can you still view, export and back up your photos if the subscription ends?
- Export. Can you get everything out in full quality, with dates, in one go, without paying?
### What are the red flags?
- Only "military-grade" or "bank-level" security, with no specifics.
- A code that the developer can reset by email, without saying what that means for privacy.
- Cloud backup only on a paid plan, so free users have one copy on one phone.
- Heavy ads, or tracking data in the privacy label.
- Recent reviews about photos disappearing after updates or new phones.
- No update in over a year. Vault apps need to keep up with each iOS release.
### How do you use a photo vault more safely?
- Use a long code, and don't reuse your iPhone passcode.
- Save your recovery phrase or key on paper, somewhere safe.
- Remove originals from Photos and Recently Deleted after importing.
- Check the backup now and then, especially before changing phones (see our new-iPhone checklist ).
- Keep a second copy of anything irreplaceable, somewhere you control.
We built Noxium, our own vault, to pass this checklist: photos are encrypted on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM using a key from your pattern (Argon2id); the backup is encrypted, in your own iCloud, on the free plan; a recovery phrase you write down at setup is the only spare key; the privacy label is Data Not Collected; there are no ads; and if Pro ends you keep full access to view, export and back up. It's also brand new, with no reviews yet, so judge it by the same checklist.
Noxium: no account, no ads, encrypted on your iPhone.
Built to pass the checklist
Encrypted on your iPhone, backed up to your own iCloud, a recovery phrase only you hold, and Data Not Collected. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Are photo vault apps safe to use?
Some are. The safe ones encrypt photos on your phone with a key only you control, keep a backup you can restore, and don't track you. Check the listing and privacy label before trusting one.
Can photo vault apps see my photos?
If the app encrypts on your phone with a key only you hold, no. If it keeps photos unencrypted, or stores them on its own servers with a key it controls, it could.
Is the iPhone Hidden album safer than a vault app?
It's safer than a vault that doesn't encrypt, but it opens with your iPhone passcode and syncs to your other devices. A good vault adds a separate code and its own encryption.
Do photo vault apps get hacked?
Weak ones can leak photos through unencrypted files or cloud accounts. With a properly encrypted vault, the risk shifts to your code: keep it long and private.

# Pattern lock: how Noxium opens with a shape, not a PIN

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/pattern-lock
Last updated: 2026-11-13

Feature
## Pattern lock: how Noxium opens with a shape, not a PIN
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 13 November 2026
Short answer
Noxium opens when you draw a pattern across at least 6 bolts on a 5×5 plate of 25 bolts. The pattern isn't a screen in front of your photos: it is turned into the key that decrypts them, and it is never stored. Face ID can open the main vault once you've set it up.
Most photo vault apps ask for a 4-digit PIN. That's 10,000 codes, and people pick birthdays and years. Noxium, the photo vault we make, uses a pattern on a larger grid instead. It is quick to draw with one thumb, hard to guess, and it is the only thing that can unlock your vault. This page explains how the pattern lock works, how to pick a strong one, and what it can't do.
### How does the pattern lock work?
Your pattern is turned into an encryption key on the iPhone, and that key unlocks the vault. Nothing compares your pattern to a saved copy, because there is no saved copy.
- You draw. The plate has 25 bolts in 5 rows of 5. A pattern must touch at least 6 of them. If your line passes straight over a bolt you haven't used yet, that bolt is added for you, as on Android pattern locks.
- The pattern becomes a key. Noxium runs the pattern through Argon2id (from libsodium) with 64 MiB of memory and 3 passes. This is slow on purpose, so every guess costs time and memory.
- The key opens the vault key. Each vault has its own random key, sealed with the pattern key using AES-256-GCM. If the seal opens, you're in. If it doesn't, nothing opens and nothing is shown.
Because the check is "does this key open a vault?", one lock screen can serve several vaults. A decoy vault simply has its own pattern. Noxium tries every vault each time, so a wrong pattern looks the same however many vaults exist. For the cryptography in plain English, see how encrypted photo vaults work and our page on on-device encryption .
### How many patterns are there?
On Noxium's 5×5 plate there are 19,174,112 different patterns that touch exactly 6 bolts. We counted them with the same drawing rules the app uses. Longer patterns add far more:
Possible codes by lock type
Lock Possible codes
4-digit PIN 10,000
6-digit PIN 1,000,000
Android 3×3 pattern (4 to 9 dots) 389,112
Noxium 5×5, exactly 6 bolts 19,174,112
Noxium 5×5, exactly 7 bolts 261,248,096
Noxium 5×5, exactly 8 bolts 3,428,210,784
These are counts of what's possible, not what people choose. Studies of Android pattern locks found that most people draw short shapes that start in a corner and move left to right and top to bottom. A shape like that is guessed long before the big numbers matter. The count only protects you if your pattern isn't an obvious one.
### How do you pick a strong pattern?
Use more than 6 bolts, change direction, and avoid letters and simple shapes. A few rules of thumb:
- Go to 8 or more bolts. Each extra bolt multiplies the number of possible patterns by roughly 13.
- Don't start in a corner. The top-left corner is the most common start on any pattern lock.
- Cross your own line. Diagonals and knight-like jumps (two across, one down) are rarer than straight runs.
- Skip letters, initials and outlines. An L, a Z, a square or your initial are the first things someone tries.
- Make it different from your iPhone passcode and any decoy pattern. Noxium refuses a pattern that already opens another vault.
### How do you set it up?
You draw your pattern the first time you open Noxium, and you can change it any time from inside the vault.
- Draw your pattern. On Set your pattern , draw across at least 6 bolts. If you use fewer, Noxium tells you how many you drew.
- Draw it again. Step 2 of 2 asks for the same pattern. If the two don't match, you start over.
- Save your recovery phrase. Setup ends with a recovery phrase , the spare key if you forget your pattern.
- Change it later. Open the vault, tap Settings › Change pattern , and draw the new one. Only the vault key's seal changes; your photos aren't re-encrypted.
The lock screen: draw across at least 6 of the 25 bolts.
### How does Face ID fit in?
Face ID is a shortcut to the main vault, not a replacement for the pattern. When you turn it on in Settings › Lock , Noxium keeps the main vault's key in the iPhone's Keychain, locked to Face ID on this device only. It never syncs to iCloud. If someone adds a new face to your iPhone, the saved key stops working and you draw your pattern again. Decoy vaults never use Face ID: they open only with their own patterns. To lock other apps and the Photos app with Face ID, see how to lock photos on iPhone .
### What doesn't the pattern lock protect?
A pattern is only as private as the moment you draw it. Be honest with yourself about these limits:
- Someone watching. Patterns are easier to see over a shoulder than a PIN. Draw it with the screen angled away, or use Face ID in public.
- Smudges. A greasy screen can show the path of a pattern you draw often. Wipe the screen now and then.
- A short or obvious pattern. The 19 million figure means nothing if your pattern is a Z.
- Being forced to open it. No lock stops someone who makes you draw it. That's what a decoy vault is for.
- An unlocked phone left open. While the vault is open, anyone holding the phone can see it. Set Settings › Lock after leaving to Immediately.
Wrong guesses are slowed down too. After 5 wrong patterns Noxium waits 30 seconds before the next try, after 10 it waits 5 minutes, and after 15 it waits 30 minutes.
### Is it free or Pro?
The pattern lock is part of every Noxium vault, free and Pro. The free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, and full iCloud backup and restore. Noxium Pro adds unlimited items and album patterns , which put a separate pattern on a single album.
A lock that is also the key
Your pattern is never stored. It is stretched with Argon2id into the key that opens your vault.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Is a pattern lock safer than a PIN?
It can be. A 6-bolt pattern on Noxium's 5×5 plate has about 19 million possibilities, against 10,000 for a 4-digit PIN. But people pick predictable patterns, so a long, irregular pattern is what makes it safer.
Is my pattern stored on the phone?
No. Noxium keeps only the vault key sealed with a key made from your pattern. When you draw, it rebuilds that key and tries to open the seal.
What happens if I draw the wrong pattern?
Nothing opens. After 5 wrong tries Noxium makes you wait 30 seconds, then 5 minutes after 10, and 30 minutes after 15.
What if I forget my pattern?
Tap Forgot your pattern? on the lock screen and enter your recovery phrase. Nobody can reset a pattern: not us, not Apple. More in forgot your photo vault password .
Can I use the same pattern on a new iPhone?
Yes. On a new iPhone signed in to the same Apple Account, choose Restore your vault and draw the same pattern. Face ID has to be turned on again there.
