# On-device encryption: what Noxium encrypts, and how

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/on-device-encryption
Last updated: 2026-11-13

Feature
## On-device encryption: what Noxium encrypts, and how
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 13 November 2026
Short answer
Noxium encrypts every photo, video and note on your iPhone before it is stored or backed up. Keys come from your pattern through Argon2id, and files are sealed with AES-256-GCM. Names, dates and places are encrypted too, and your pattern is never stored.
Many photo vault apps show a PIN screen in front of ordinary image files. If someone gets at those files another way, through a computer backup, a forensic tool or a bug, the photos are just there. An encrypted photo vault app stores only scrambled data, so a copy of the files is useless without your key. This page explains exactly what Noxium, the vault we make, encrypts on your iPhone, with which tools, and where the protection stops.
### How does Noxium's encryption work?
Noxium uses keys inside keys. Your pattern makes one key, that key opens a vault key, and the vault key opens a separate key for every file. Here is the chain, from your finger to a photo:
- Pattern key. When you draw your pattern , Argon2id (from libsodium) stretches it into a 256-bit key, using 64 MiB of memory and 3 passes and a random salt. The slowness is the point: each guess costs real time and memory.
- Vault key. Each vault has its own random 256-bit key. It is stored only sealed by the pattern key, with AES-256-GCM from Apple's CryptoKit.
- File keys. Every photo, video and note gets its own random key, sealed by the vault key. Thumbnails use a separate key derived from the file key.
- The file itself. Each file is encrypted with AES-256-GCM in 1 MiB chunks, each with its own authentication tag. A long video can play without decrypting the whole file first, and a changed or damaged chunk fails to open instead of showing corrupted data.
Changing your pattern only re-seals the vault key, so it takes a moment even with thousands of photos. Your recovery phrase is a second seal on the same vault key. For the ideas behind this, without math, read how encrypted photo vaults work .
### What exactly is encrypted?
Everything you put in a vault, plus the details about it. That matters, because a list of file names and dates can say a lot on its own.
What Noxium encrypts on the iPhone
Data Encrypted?
Photos, videos, Live Photos Yes, AES-256-GCM, one key per file
Thumbnails and previews Yes, with their own derived key
Names, dates and places Yes
Album names and notes Yes
Your pattern Never stored at all
The iCloud backup Yes, only already-encrypted data is uploaded
On disk, vault files carry random names and use iOS's strongest file protection class, so they are also locked by iOS while the iPhone is locked. They are left out of the iPhone's own backup on purpose; Noxium makes its own encrypted iCloud backup instead.
### What about photos added from the share sheet?
They are encrypted before Noxium's main app even opens. When you use Send to Noxium from another app, the share extension encrypts each file with a new key and seals that key to a public key. The extension never holds your vault key. The next time you unlock, Noxium opens the envelope and moves the file into your vault.
### How do you turn it on?
You don't need to. Encryption is always on, for every vault and every item, free or Pro.
- Set your pattern. The first time you open Noxium, draw a pattern across at least 6 bolts. This creates your first vault and its key.
- Add photos. Import from Photos, take them with the built-in camera, or use Send to Noxium . Each item is encrypted as it is added.
- Remove the originals. Copies left in the Photos app aren't protected. Turn on Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos (see import and export ) so Noxium offers to delete them after an import, then empty Collections › Utilities › Recently Deleted in Photos.
Encryption happens on the iPhone first. Only the encrypted result is backed up.
### What doesn't encryption protect?
Encryption protects files at rest. It can't protect a photo while you're looking at it, or a copy outside the vault.
- An open vault. While it is unlocked, anyone holding the phone sees what you see. Use Settings › Lock after leaving and Lock when face down .
- A weak pattern. Argon2id slows guessing, but a Z-shaped pattern is still guessed quickly.
- Copies elsewhere. Originals still in Photos or iCloud Photos, screenshots, and files you export are not encrypted by Noxium.
- A compromised iPhone. Spyware, or a jailbroken phone running hostile code, can see the screen while the vault is open.
- Being forced. If someone makes you draw your pattern, encryption doesn't help. A decoy vault does.
Vault content is hidden in the app switcher and during screen recording, which covers casual glances. No iPhone app can block a screenshot; see photo vault screenshot protection . It isn't a defense against spyware.
### Is it free or Pro?
Encryption is the same on every plan. The free plan holds 150 photos, 10 videos and unlimited notes, with full iCloud backup and restore. Noxium Pro adds unlimited items, emergency erase, iPhone and iPad sync, custom icons, album patterns and shared vaults. If Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault.
Encryption you can read about
Argon2id for your pattern, AES-256-GCM for every file, and only ciphertext in your own iCloud.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Are photo vault apps on iPhone encrypted?
Some are, many aren't. Look for a named cipher such as AES-256, encryption on the device before backup, and no password reset by email. Our guide are photo vault apps safe? has a checklist.
Can the developer see my photos?
No. Noxium has no accounts and no servers that hold your photos. The keys come from your pattern on your iPhone, and the backup in your iCloud is already encrypted.
Isn't the iPhone already encrypted?
Yes, iOS encrypts the whole phone, but it unlocks with your iPhone passcode. Anyone who knows the passcode, or a backup made from the phone, can see your Photos library. Noxium adds a second lock with a key only your pattern makes.
What is AES-256-GCM?
AES with a 256-bit key is the standard cipher used across the industry. GCM adds a tag that detects any change to the encrypted data, so damaged or altered files don't open.
Does encryption make Noxium slow?
Unlocking takes a moment on purpose, because Argon2id is slow by design. Browsing is quick: thumbnails come first, and videos decrypt in 1 MiB chunks as they play.

# Encrypted iCloud backup: your vault, in your iCloud, unreadable to anyone else

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/encrypted-icloud-backup
Last updated: 2026-11-13

Feature
## Encrypted iCloud backup: your vault, in your iCloud, unreadable to anyone else
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 13 November 2026
Short answer
Noxium backs up an encrypted copy of your vault to your own private iCloud (CloudKit). Only encrypted data leaves the iPhone, so Apple stores it but can't read it. On a new iPhone, draw your pattern and the vault restores. Backup and restore are included in the free plan.
A photo vault without a backup is one dropped phone away from losing everything. A backup that isn't encrypted defeats the point of a vault. Noxium, the vault we make, does both: it keeps its own backup in your iCloud, and everything in it is encrypted on your iPhone first. There is no Noxium account and no Noxium server in between. This page shows what is uploaded, how restoring works, and what the backup can't do.
### How does the encrypted backup work?
Noxium encrypts each item on the iPhone, then uploads only that encrypted data to the private CloudKit database in your iCloud. Apple's servers hold it, but the keys stay with your pattern.
- Encrypt first. Every photo, video, note and thumbnail is already encrypted with AES-256-GCM by the time it is stored (see on-device encryption ). The backup reuses that ciphertext.
- Upload to your iCloud. Each vault gets its own space in your private iCloud database. It holds the vault's sealed key, its encrypted details, and its encrypted items.
- Keep going while locked. Because the backup only handles encrypted data, uploads continue after you lock the vault.
- Restore with your pattern. On a new iPhone, your pattern rebuilds the key that opens the vault key in iCloud. Nothing else can.
The backup is separate from the iPhone's own iCloud Backup. Noxium deliberately leaves its vault files out of the device backup and Quick Start transfers, so private photos don't sit in an ordinary backup. Its own encrypted backup is what brings them back.
### What goes to iCloud, and what doesn't?
What Noxium uploads to your private iCloud
Data In iCloud?
Photos, videos, notes, thumbnails Yes, encrypted
Names, dates, places, album names Yes, encrypted
Each vault's key Only sealed by your pattern (and recovery phrase)
The salt and Argon2id settings Yes, so a new iPhone can rebuild your key
Your pattern or recovery phrase No, never
Face ID key No, it stays in this iPhone's Keychain
This holds with or without Apple's Advanced Data Protection. With standard iCloud protection, Apple can decrypt your iCloud Backup and iCloud Photos (Apple lists the categories in its iCloud data security overview ). Noxium's backup is different: Apple only ever receives data that is already encrypted with a key it doesn't have.
### How do you set it up and check it?
Turn it on during setup, then check it before you change phones.
- Turn it on. During setup, choose Back up to iCloud . Your iPhone must be signed in to iCloud. You can turn it on later in Settings › iCloud backup › Back up this vault .
- Check the status. Settings › iCloud backup shows when the vault was last backed up and how many items are waiting. Tap Back up now to start right away.
- Choose how videos upload. Wi-Fi only for videos is on by default, so large videos wait for Wi-Fi.
- Back up each vault. A decoy vault has its own backup switch. The status only counts the vault you're in, so it never reveals that other vaults exist.
- Watch your storage. The backup counts toward your iCloud storage. Used in iCloud shows how much. If iCloud is full, Noxium pauses and tells you about how much more space it needs. See why a photo vault takes up storage .
Only encrypted data leaves the iPhone. It is stored in your private iCloud.
### How do you restore on a new iPhone?
Sign in to the same Apple Account, open Noxium, and draw your pattern. The full checklist is in how to move a photo vault to a new iPhone .
- Find the backup. On first launch, Noxium looks for a backup in your iCloud and shows Restore your vault .
- Draw your pattern. Draw the pattern you used on your old iPhone, or choose Restore with recovery phrase .
- Browse right away. Details and thumbnails arrive first. Choose whether full-size photos download Now or When I open them .
- Open the other vaults. Other vaults, such as a decoy, stay in iCloud until you draw their patterns. Later, use Settings › iCloud backup › Restore from iCloud .
Short on space? Free up space removes full-size copies that are already backed up. Previews stay, and the originals download again when you open them.
### What doesn't the backup protect?
- Forgetting both keys. If you lose your pattern and your recovery phrase , nobody can open the backup: not us, not Apple.
- Someone in your iCloud with time to guess. Your iCloud holds the sealed keys and the salt. A person who gets into your Apple Account could try patterns offline. Argon2id makes every guess slow, but a short or obvious pattern can still fall. Protect your Apple Account with a strong password and two-factor authentication.
- What Apple can see. Apple can see that Noxium stores data in your iCloud, and roughly how much. It can't see the photos or their details.
- Deleting the backup. The backup lives in your iCloud. If the Apple Account is lost or the data is deleted, the backup is gone too. Turning off Back up this vault stops new uploads; what's already in iCloud stays.
- Live sync. The backup restores a vault; keeping an iPhone and an iPad in step is a separate Pro feature.
### Is it free or Pro?
Full iCloud backup and restore is part of the free plan, which holds 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes and 1 decoy vault. Noxium Pro adds unlimited items and iPhone and iPad sync , among other things. If Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault.
New phone? Everything comes back.
An encrypted backup goes to your own private iCloud. On a new iPhone, draw your pattern and your vault restores.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Do photo vault apps back up to iCloud?
Some do, some use their own cloud, and some keep photos only on the phone. Check the app's settings for a backup section before you rely on it. Noxium backs up to your own iCloud, encrypted.
Will my vault photos show up in iCloud Photos?
No. Noxium's backup sits in its own private CloudKit space, not in iCloud Photos, and it is encrypted. Nothing appears in the Photos app or on iCloud.com. Apple's Hidden album is a different case: see is the iPhone Hidden album private?
Does the backup use my iCloud storage?
Yes. It counts toward your iCloud plan. Settings › iCloud backup shows how much it uses, and Noxium tells you if iCloud is full.
Can I restore with a different Apple Account?
No. The backup lives in the iCloud of the Apple Account that made it, so the new iPhone must be signed in to that account.
Do I need Advanced Data Protection?
Not for Noxium's backup, which is encrypted before upload either way. Advanced Data Protection is still worth turning on for the rest of your iCloud, such as Photos and device backups.

# Recovery phrase: the spare key only you hold

URL: https://getnoxium.app/features/recovery-phrase
Last updated: 2026-11-13

Feature
## Recovery phrase: the spare key only you hold
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 13 November 2026
Short answer
At setup, Noxium gives you a recovery phrase to write down. If you forget your pattern, the phrase opens your main vault, on this iPhone or a new one. Nobody can reset a pattern: not the developer, not Apple. So the phrase is the only spare key.
A vault that can be reset by email is a vault someone else can open. A vault with no way back punishes one bad day of memory. Noxium, the photo vault we make, sits in between: there is no reset, but there is a spare key that only you hold. This page explains how the recovery phrase works, how to make and store it, and what happens if you lose it.
### How does the recovery phrase work?
The phrase is a second way to make the key that opens your vault. Your pattern and your phrase each seal the same vault key, so either one opens it.
- A generated phrase is 8 words. Noxium picks them at random from the 2,048-word BIP-39 English list, the same list many crypto wallets use. That's 88 bits of randomness, far more than any pattern.
- It becomes a key the same way your pattern does. Argon2id (libsodium) stretches it, with 64 MiB of memory and 3 passes, into a key that seals your vault key with AES-256-GCM.
- It is never stored. Like your pattern , the phrase isn't kept anywhere by Noxium. Only the sealed vault key is, on your iPhone and in your encrypted iCloud backup .
- Case and spacing don't matter. "Author Tuition" and "author tuition" are read the same, so a phrase copied from paper still works.
Because the phrase opens the vault key itself, it works without the old phone, and without us. For how keys inside keys work, see how encrypted photo vaults work .
### How do you set it up?
The phrase is the last step of setup, and you can replace it any time.
- Get your phrase. On Recovery phrase , keep Generated to use 8 random words. Tap New phrase if you'd like different ones.
- Or choose your own. Tap Your own and type 6 to 9 words, at least 20 characters in all. A phrase you make up is easier to remember and easier to guess, so avoid song lyrics and quotes.
- Write it down on paper. Copy and Save to Files exist, but a copied phrase leaves the clipboard after 2 minutes and a saved file isn't encrypted.
- Pass the quick check. Tap I've saved it . For a generated phrase, Noxium asks for a word or two, such as "Which is word 3 of your phrase?", so you know your copy is right.
- Replace it later. Inside the vault, open Settings › Recovery phrase and tap Make a new recovery phrase or Choose my own phrase . The new phrase replaces the old one, which stops working.
Step 5 of setup: eight random words. Write them down on paper.
### How do you use it if you forget your pattern?
Tap Forgot your pattern? on the lock screen and type the phrase. It opens your main vault.
- On the same iPhone: on the lock screen, tap Forgot your pattern? , enter the phrase in Use your recovery phrase , and the main vault opens.
- Set a new pattern: once you're in, go to Settings › Change pattern .
- On a new iPhone: sign in to the same Apple Account, open Noxium, and on Restore your vault choose Restore with recovery phrase .
Locked out of a different app? Our guide on what to do if you forgot your photo vault password covers how other vaults handle it.
### Where should you keep it?
On paper, somewhere safe, away from the phone. Some practical choices:
- A place you'd keep a passport. A drawer or a document folder at home, not your wallet or phone case.
- A password manager, if you already use one well. It's encrypted and backed up. Don't put it in a plain note, an email to yourself, or a photo.
- Not inside the vault. The phrase is for when you can't get in.
- Never share it. Anyone with the phrase can open your main vault without your pattern.
### What doesn't the recovery phrase protect?
- Losing both. If you forget your pattern and lose the phrase, nobody can open the vault: not us, not Apple. That's the cost of a vault no one else can open.
- A phrase someone finds. A phrase on paper is only as safe as where you keep it. If you think someone saw it, make a new one.
- Other vaults. The phrase from setup opens your main vault only. A decoy vault opens with its own pattern, or with a phrase you make for it in that vault's Settings.
- A deleted app with no backup. The phrase opens a vault that still exists, on the phone or in iCloud. If the app is deleted and there's no backup, there's nothing left to open.
### Is it free or Pro?
The recovery phrase is part of every Noxium vault, free and Pro. The free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault, and full iCloud backup and restore.
Never locked out, never reset by anyone else
You write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault. Nobody can reset a pattern: not the developer, not Apple.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
What is a recovery phrase in a photo vault?
A set of words you save at setup that can open the vault if you forget your code. Unlike an email reset, only the person holding the words can use it.
Can I see my recovery phrase again later?
No. Noxium doesn't store it, so it can't show it again. If you've lost your copy, make a new one in Settings › Recovery phrase while you can still open the vault.
Does changing my pattern change the phrase?
No. The pattern and the phrase are two separate keys to the same vault. Changing one leaves the other working.
Is it the same as a crypto wallet seed phrase?
It uses the same BIP-39 word list, but it isn't a wallet seed and can't be used for one. Treat it with the same care.
Can Noxium's developer recover my vault?
No. We never have your pattern, your phrase or your keys. That's why the phrase matters.
Something wrong or out of date? Email business@inertiaprojects.info and we'll fix it.

- On-device encryption

# Privault review: how it compares with Noxium in 2026

URL: https://getnoxium.app/compare/privault
Last updated: 2026-11-14

Compare
## Privault review: how it compares with Noxium in 2026
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 14 November 2026
Short answer
Privault is a popular, long-running vault with a keypad lock, a second passcode for a decoy folder and an erase-all passcode. Its App Store listing doesn't name a cipher or describe any backup, and the app hasn't been updated since 28 February 2025. Pick Privault for its media player and Wi-Fi transfer; pick Noxium if you want named encryption, an encrypted backup in your own iCloud and no data used to track you.
Privault, from Binspir Technologies, has been on the App Store since January 2017 and has 76,566 US ratings at 4.7 stars. It's one of the vaults people find first when they search for a private photo vault. This review looks at what Privault offers, using its App Store listing checked on 14 November 2026, and compares it point by point with Noxium. We make Noxium, so weigh what we say about it accordingly; everything about Privault below comes from Privault's own listing.
### Noxium vs Privault at a glance
Source: each app's US App Store listing, checked 14 November 2026. Noxium: our published facts.
Noxium Privault
Account needed No Not in listing
Opens with Pattern on a 5×5 plate; Face ID optional Digit passcode on a keypad
Encryption named AES-256-GCM, key from your pattern (Argon2id) Says storage is encrypted; cipher not named
Backup Your own iCloud, encrypted, free Not in listing; export to Camera Roll or over Wi-Fi
Decoy Yes, 1 free Secondary passcode opens a secondary folder
Panic erase Emergency erase pattern (Pro) Erase-all passcode
Forgot your code Recovery phrase you write down at setup Not in listing
Ads None Sells a "Remove ADs" purchase ($2.99)

For 17 vault apps side by side, see our photo vault comparison .
### What does Privault do well, and where does it fall short?
Privault does a lot with media and offers three passcodes for different situations. Its weak points are what the listing leaves out: the cipher, a backup, and recovery.
#### What Privault does well
- Three passcodes. The primary passcode opens your files. A secondary passcode opens a separate folder, which the listing suggests giving out if someone threatens you. An erase-all passcode deletes all hidden files when you decide you have to.
- Media support. The listing says its player handles about 150 video formats, including MKV, AVI and WMV, and its photo browser reads HEIC, TIFF and more.
- A built-in voice recorder for private audio notes, set up from the keypad.
- Wi-Fi transfer. An embedded Wi-Fi server lets you move files to and from a computer, as well as through the Camera Roll.
- A one-time price. Permanent Pro is $45.99, so you don't have to subscribe.
- Old devices. It runs on iOS 11 and later and supports iPad.
#### Where Privault falls short
- No named encryption. The listing says the "encrypted storage" opens with your passcode, but it doesn't say how files are encrypted or how the passcode becomes a key. A short digit passcode is also far easier to guess than a long one, unless the app slows guessing down.
- No backup described. The listing doesn't mention iCloud or any cloud backup. If the phone is lost or the app is deleted, assume the only copies were on that phone, unless you exported them.
- No recovery described. The listing doesn't say what happens if you forget the passcode.
- Tracking. Its privacy label lists data used to track you and data linked to you.
- Not recently updated. The last update was 28 February 2025, more than 20 months before we checked. That isn't proof of a problem, but long gaps between updates can matter for an app that holds private files.
### How are Privault and Noxium different?
The real differences are in what's documented: how files are encrypted, where the backup lives, and what happens when you forget your code.
#### Encryption
Noxium names every piece. Your pattern is turned into a key with Argon2id, and every photo, video and note is encrypted on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, including names, dates and places. The pattern itself is never stored. Our page on on-device encryption lists every layer. Privault's listing says its storage is encrypted, and stops there. If encryption matters to you, ask any vault to name its cipher; how encrypted photo vaults work explains what to look for.
#### Backup and moving to a new phone
Noxium keeps an encrypted backup in your own private iCloud, on the free plan too. On a new iPhone you draw your pattern and the vault restores. Privault's listing describes no backup; it offers export to the Camera Roll and a Wi-Fi server for copying files to a computer. That works as a manual backup, but the copies leave the vault unencrypted.
#### Decoys and panic erase
Both apps have a second code for a harmless space. Privault's secondary passcode opens a secondary folder; Noxium's second pattern opens a separate decoy vault, and the free plan includes 1. Both also have a way to erase: Privault's erase-all passcode, and Noxium's emergency erase pattern (Pro), which opens a harmless vault and erases the others. Read what a decoy vault is before you rely on one.
#### Forgetting your code
Noxium has no reset, by design. At setup you write down a recovery phrase, and it opens your vault if you forget your pattern. Privault's listing doesn't describe recovery, so contact its developer (support@binspir.com) before you need it.
#### Price and privacy
Both are free to start, with a one-time option. Privault's Permanent Pro is $45.99; Noxium Pro is $39.99 once. Noxium has no ads, no accounts and no analytics, and its privacy label is Data Not Collected. Privault sells a $2.99 purchase to remove ads, and its label lists data used to track you.
### Which should you choose?
- Pick Privault if you need to play many video formats, move files over Wi-Fi to a computer, record private voice notes, or use an iPhone older than iOS 17.
- Pick Noxium if you want encryption that's named and documented, an encrypted backup in your own iCloud that restores with your pattern, a recovery phrase, and no ads or tracking.
### How do you switch from Privault without losing photos?
Export from Privault, check the copies, import them into the new vault, and only then delete anything. Privault's listing says you can export through the Camera Roll or its Wi-Fi server.
- Count what you have. Note how many photos and videos are in each Privault folder, including the secondary folder.
- Export to the Camera Roll from inside Privault, folder by folder. For large videos, the Wi-Fi server to a computer may be quicker.
- Check the copies in Photos: counts match, videos play, quality is full size.
- Import into Noxium. Turn on Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos so it offers to remove the copies from Photos after import. Then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
- Check the backup in Settings › iCloud backup : nothing waiting.
- Only then delete files from Privault, and cancel any subscription in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Exported photos sit unencrypted in your Photos library until the new vault imports them. Do the move in one sitting, on a phone only you are using. More tips: moving a vault without losing photos .
Encryption you can read about
Noxium encrypts everything on your iPhone with AES-256-GCM and backs up only encrypted data to your own iCloud. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.

### Questions people ask
Is Privault safe?
It hides files behind a passcode and says its storage is encrypted, but its listing doesn't name the cipher, describe a backup or explain recovery, and it was last updated on 28 February 2025. Our checklist in are photo vault apps safe? covers what to check.
Is Privault free?
Yes, to download. On the US App Store, Pro costs $3.49 a month, $24.99 a year or $45.99 once, and removing ads is a $2.99 purchase.
Does Privault back up to iCloud?
Its App Store listing doesn't mention iCloud or any cloud backup. It describes export to the Camera Roll and a Wi-Fi server for copying files to a computer.
What is Privault's secondary passcode?
A second passcode that opens a separate folder instead of your main files. The listing suggests giving it out if someone forces you to open the app.
What if I forget my Privault passcode?
The listing doesn't describe recovery. Don't delete the app, and contact the developer at support@binspir.com. Our guide to a forgotten vault password explains what's safe to try.

# Keepsafe review: how it compares with Noxium in 2026

URL: https://getnoxium.app/compare/keepsafe
Last updated: 2026-11-14

Compare
## Keepsafe review: how it compares with Noxium in 2026
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 14 November 2026
Short answer
Keepsafe is a polished, actively updated vault that syncs across iPhone and Android through an email account and its own Private Cloud. Its free plan is supported by ads, and Premium is a subscription. Pick Keepsafe if you want an email account to recover through and Android support; pick Noxium if you want no account, a backup encrypted in your own iCloud and a one-time price.
Keepsafe has been on the App Store since April 2012 and has 386,264 US ratings at 4.7 stars, which makes it one of the best-known photo vaults there is. This review looks at what Keepsafe does well and where it falls short, using its App Store listing (checked on 14 November 2026) and its help center, then compares it with Noxium. We make Noxium, so weigh what we say about our own app accordingly.
Already decided to leave Keepsafe? Our list of Keepsafe alternatives with no account compares four of them, and Vaultaire vs Keepsafe covers that pair.
### Noxium vs Keepsafe at a glance
Source: each app's US App Store listing, checked 14 November 2026, and the Keepsafe Help Center. Noxium: our published facts.
Noxium Keepsafe
Account needed No Yes, an email account
Opens with Pattern on a 5×5 plate; Face ID optional PIN; Touch ID (listing)
Encryption named AES-256-GCM, key from your pattern (Argon2id) Listing: "military-grade". Help center: AES-256
Backup Your own iCloud, encrypted, free Keepsafe's Private Cloud: first 200 items free, up to 10,000 with Premium
Platforms iPhone and iPad iPhone, iPad and Android, synced through your account
Decoy Yes, 1 free Not in listing (the help center has a decoy vault article)
Forgot your code Recovery phrase you write down at setup Through your email account
Ads None Free plan is ad-supported; Premium is ad-free

Last update 13 November 2026 12 November 2026
### What does Keepsafe do well, and where does it fall short?
Keepsafe is mature, well designed and works across platforms. Its trade-offs come from the account, the company cloud and the ads.
#### What Keepsafe does well
- It's actively maintained. Version 13.36.0 came out on 12 November 2026.
- Android and iPhone. The listing says your items sync to all your Keepsafe installations on any platform. If you switch between iPhone and Android, that's rare among vaults.
- Recovery through email. Because there's an account, there's a way back in if you forget your PIN, and the help center explains what to do if you lose access to that email.
- Useful extras. Album Lock gives single albums their own PIN (Premium), Safe Send shares a photo for a limited time, and Trash Recovery brings back items you deleted by mistake (Premium).
- Space Saver. Premium can keep small copies on the phone and the originals in the cloud, which frees space on a full iPhone.
- A built-in camera , albums, slideshows, and iPad support.
#### Where Keepsafe falls short
- An account and a company cloud. Your vault is tied to an email address, and your backup lives on Keepsafe's servers, not in your own iCloud.
- Vague encryption claims in the listing. "Military-grade" says little; the help center is more specific and names AES-256.
- Ads on the free plan , and its privacy label lists data used to track you.
- Subscription only. The listing shows monthly and yearly Premium, with no lifetime option, and the free plan backs up only your first 200 items.
- Space Saver's catch. With it on, the full-size originals exist only in Keepsafe's cloud. Leaving later means downloading them first.
### How are Keepsafe and Noxium different?
The main difference is who holds your account and your backup. With Keepsafe, the company does. With Noxium, there is no account, and the backup sits in your own iCloud, encrypted with a key only your pattern makes.
#### Account and recovery
Keepsafe signs you in with an email address, which gives you a reset path. Noxium has no account and no reset by anyone, including us or Apple. Instead, you write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault if you forget your pattern. Lose both and nobody can open the vault, which is also why nobody else can.
#### Backup
Keepsafe backs up to its Private Cloud: the first 200 items on the free plan, up to 10,000 with Premium. Noxium backs up everything, free, to your own private iCloud, and only encrypted data leaves the phone. See encrypted iCloud backup for what's uploaded and how restore works.
#### Encryption
Both say they use AES-256. Noxium names the whole chain: Argon2id turns your pattern into a key, every file is sealed with AES-256-GCM on the iPhone, and names, dates and places are encrypted too. With Keepsafe, a copy of your files also lives on the company's servers, tied to your account.
#### Decoys and lock
Noxium opens with a pattern across a 5×5 plate, and a second pattern opens a separate decoy vault, 1 on the free plan. Keepsafe opens with a PIN, and its listing mentions Touch ID. Its listing doesn't mention a decoy, though its help center has an article about moving content out of a "Decoy Vault".
#### Price and privacy
Over a year, Keepsafe Premium is $23.99; Noxium Pro is $17.99. Noxium also sells Pro once for $39.99; Keepsafe's listing shows no lifetime plan. Noxium has no ads and no analytics, and its privacy label is Data Not Collected.
### Which should you choose?
- Pick Keepsafe if you use Android too, you want an email account to recover through, or you want Space Saver to free up phone storage.
- Pick Noxium if you don't want an account or a company cloud, you want your backup in your own iCloud, encrypted, and you'd rather pay once than subscribe.
### How do you switch from Keepsafe without losing photos?
Export from Keepsafe to your Photos library, check everything arrived at full quality, import it into the new vault, and only then delete Keepsafe's copies.
- Mind Space Saver. If you use it, the originals are in Keepsafe's cloud. Make sure what you export is full size: export a few photos first and check them before you go on.
- Export album by album. Keepsafe's help center describes it: open an album, select the items, tap the send icon at the bottom left, and choose Export to Camera Roll .
- Check the export in Photos: counts match, videos play, and a few photos open at full size. Exported photos return to the date they were taken, so look further back in your library.
- Import into Noxium with Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos turned on. Then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
- Check Noxium's backup in Settings › iCloud backup .
- Only then delete items from Keepsafe and cancel Premium in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Exported photos sit unencrypted in your Photos library until the new vault imports them. Do the move in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.
No account. Your own iCloud.
Noxium opens with a pattern only you know and backs up, encrypted, to your own iCloud. Free for 150 photos and 10 videos.

Is Keepsafe safe to use?
It's a long-running, actively updated app, and its help center says it encrypts files with AES-256. The trade-off is that your account and your cloud copy sit with Keepsafe, and the free plan shows ads. Our checklist: are photo vault apps safe?
Is Keepsafe free?
It has a free, ad-supported plan that backs up your first 200 items. Premium costs $9.99 a month or $23.99 a year on the US App Store in November 2026.
Does Keepsafe store my photos on its servers?
Its backup does. Private Cloud stores your backed-up items with Keepsafe, and with Space Saver on, the full-size originals are only there.
Does Keepsafe work on Android?
Yes. Its listing says items sync to your Keepsafe installations on any platform, through your account. Noxium is for iPhone and iPad only.
How do I get my photos out of Keepsafe?
Select them in an album, tap the send icon and choose Export to Camera Roll. If you use Space Saver, check that the exported photos are full size.

# Private Photo Vault review: how it compares with Noxium

## Private Photo Vault review: how it compares with Noxium
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 14 November 2026
Short answer
Private Photo Vault (Pic Safe) is the most-reviewed vault on the US App Store, with over a million ratings, a break-in report, a decoy password and a private browser. Its encrypted Cloud Vault backup is a Premium feature in its own cloud; the free version doesn't back up. Pick it for its features and track record; pick Noxium if you want a free encrypted backup in your own iCloud and no data used to track you.
Private Photo Vault, from Legendary Software Labs, has been on the App Store since February 2011. With 1,019,778 US ratings at 4.8 stars, it's the most familiar name in photo vaults. This review covers what it does well and where it falls short, from its App Store listing checked on 14 November 2026, and compares it with Noxium. We make Noxium, so weigh what we say about our own app accordingly.
### Noxium vs Private Photo Vault at a glance
Source: each app's US App Store listing, checked 14 November 2026. Noxium: our published facts.
Noxium Private Photo Vault
Account needed No Not in listing; Cloud Vault needs a Cloud Vault Password
Opens with Pattern on a 5×5 plate; Face ID optional PIN or pattern lock
Encryption named AES-256-GCM on the device, key from your pattern (Argon2id) Cloud backup called "encrypted"; cipher not named
Backup Your own iCloud, encrypted, free Cloud Vault in its own cloud, Premium only
Decoy Yes, 1 free Decoy password
Break-in report No Photo + GPS of break-in attempts

For 17 vault apps in one table, see the full photo vault comparison .
### What does Private Photo Vault do well, and where does it fall short?
It has more features than almost any vault and a 15-year track record. Its gaps are in what's free and in what the listing says about encryption on the phone.
#### What Private Photo Vault does well
- Track record. On the App Store since 2011, still updated (version 30.0 came out on 12 November 2026), and rated 4.8 by over a million people.
- Choice of lock. A PIN or a pattern, plus a separate password for individual albums.
- Break-in report. The listing describes a photo plus GPS location of break-in attempts. Noxium doesn't have this.
- Decoy password and face-down lock , for when someone grabs the phone or makes you open it.
- A Cloud Vault that the company can't read. The listing says your Cloud Vault Password is never backed up to its servers and is what encrypts your files, so its employees can't view them.
- Extras : a private web browser that saves straight to the vault, wireless transfer, iTunes syncing, and iPad support.
#### Where Private Photo Vault falls short
- No backup on the free version. The listing says so directly and asks free users to back up their own photos. Lose the phone and the vault goes with it.
- Encryption on the phone isn't described. The listing describes the Cloud Vault as encrypted but says nothing about how files stored on the iPhone are protected, beyond the passcode.
- Its own cloud, not yours. Cloud Vault backups live with the developer, protected by your Cloud Vault Password. Forget that password and the listing says you can't view your Cloud Vault data.
- Tracking. Its privacy label lists data used to track you and data linked to you.
- Unclear pricing. The listing shows Premium purchases from $6.99 to $39.99 without saying which is which.
### How are Private Photo Vault and Noxium different?
The biggest difference is the backup: Noxium's is free and goes to your own iCloud, while Private Photo Vault's is Premium and goes to its own cloud. After that, it's how much each says about encryption, and what each tracks.
#### Backup and restore
Noxium backs up everything to your own private iCloud on the free plan, and only encrypted data leaves the phone. On a new iPhone you draw your pattern and the vault restores; see encrypted iCloud backup . Private Photo Vault's Cloud Vault also encrypts with a secret only you know, which is good, but it needs Premium and lives on the developer's servers.
#### Encryption on the phone
Noxium encrypts every photo, video and note on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, with a key made from your pattern through Argon2id. Names, dates and places are encrypted too, and the pattern is never stored. Private Photo Vault's listing names no cipher and doesn't describe encryption of the files on the phone. Our page on on-device encryption explains why that part matters.
#### Locks, decoys and alerts
Both offer a pattern lock, a decoy and a face-down lock. Private Photo Vault adds a break-in report and per-album passwords. Noxium adds album patterns (Pro) and an emergency erase pattern (Pro), which opens a harmless vault and erases the others.
#### Forgetting your code
Noxium can't be reset by anyone. You write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault on this iPhone or a new one. Private Photo Vault's listing warns that a forgotten Cloud Vault Password means losing access to that cloud data; it doesn't describe recovery for the app lock itself.
#### Price and privacy
Noxium Pro is $2.99 a week, $17.99 a year or $39.99 once, and the free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos and full backup. Noxium has no ads, no accounts and no analytics; its privacy label is Data Not Collected.
### Which should you choose?
- Pick Private Photo Vault if you want a break-in report, a private browser, a long track record, or an iPhone on iOS 15 or 16.
- Pick Noxium if you want a free encrypted backup in your own iCloud, encryption on the phone that's named and documented, a recovery phrase, and no data used to track you.
### How do you switch from Private Photo Vault without losing photos?
Export to the Photos app, check the copies, import them into the new vault, and only then delete anything. Private Photo Vault's listing says it can import from and export to the Photos app.
- Count what you have in each album, including any album with its own password and the decoy.
- Export each album to Photos from inside Private Photo Vault. If you use Cloud Vault with Space Saver, make sure the full-size originals are on the phone first.
- Check the copies in Photos: counts match, videos play, photos are full size.
- Import into Noxium. With Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos on, it offers to remove the copies from Photos. Then empty Recently Deleted .
- Check the backup in Noxium's Settings › iCloud backup .
- Only then delete from Private Photo Vault and cancel Premium in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Photos you export are unencrypted in your library until the new vault imports them. Move them in one sitting, on a phone only you are using. More on this in moving a vault without losing photos .
Backup included. In your own iCloud.
Noxium backs up an encrypted copy of your vault to your own iCloud, on the free plan. On a new iPhone, draw your pattern and it restores.

It's a long-running, actively updated app with a Cloud Vault the company says it can't read. Its listing doesn't describe encryption of files on the phone, the free version has no backup, and its privacy label lists data used to track you. See are photo vault apps safe?

Only with Premium. Its listing says the free version doesn't back up to Cloud Vault and asks you to keep your own backups.

Its listing says you won't be able to view your Cloud Vault data, because the password is never stored on its servers. Write it down somewhere safe.

# Vaultaire review: how it compares with Noxium in 2026

URL: https://getnoxium.app/compare/vaultaire
Last updated: 2026-11-14

Compare
## Vaultaire review: how it compares with Noxium in 2026
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 14 November 2026
Short answer
Vaultaire is a well-built, encrypted vault: AES-256-GCM, a 5×5 pattern lock, no account, decoy vaults and an encrypted iCloud backup on its free plan. Noxium works the same way on those points. Pick Vaultaire for 3 free vaults, 31 languages and family plans; pick Noxium for a bigger free plan, Argon2id key stretching, cheaper yearly Pro and a Data Not Collected privacy label.
Vaultaire, from Wraxle LLC, came to the App Store in March 2026 and has 65 US ratings at 4.7 stars. Of all the vaults we compare, it's the one most like Noxium: both encrypt on the iPhone, both open with a pattern on a 5×5 grid, and both back up to your own iCloud without an account. That makes the differences smaller and more technical. We make Noxium, so weigh what we say about our own app accordingly. Everything about Vaultaire here comes from its App Store listing (checked 14 November 2026) and its own feature pages.
### Noxium vs Vaultaire at a glance
Source: each app's US App Store listing, checked 14 November 2026, and vaultaire.app. Noxium: our published facts.
Noxium Vaultaire
Account needed No No
Opens with Pattern across 6+ of 25 bolts (5×5); Face ID optional Pattern across 6+ of 25 dots (5×5)
File encryption AES-256-GCM AES-256-GCM
Pattern to key Argon2id, 64 MiB, 3 passes PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 600,000 iterations
Backup Your own iCloud, encrypted, free Your own iCloud, encrypted, free; on by default
Free plan 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes, 1 decoy vault Up to 3 vaults, 100 photos and 10 videos in total
Panic option (Pro) Emergency erase: erases the other vaults Duress vault: removes access to the other vaults on this device
Recovery 8-word phrase (BIP-39 words), shown once 9-word sentence, viewable later in settings
Price (US) Pro $2.99/week, $17.99/year or $39.99 once Pro $1.99/week, $5.99/month, $19.99/year or $39.99 lifetime; family plans $49.99/year or $99.99 lifetime
Privacy label Data Not Collected Data Linked to You; Data Not Linked to You (none used to track you)
App languages 16 31
US ratings None yet (released November 2026) 65, 4.7★
### What does Vaultaire do well, and where does it fall short?
Vaultaire gets the important things right: real encryption on the device, no account, a free encrypted backup and decoys. Its trade-offs are a smaller free plan, a faster-to-compute key derivation, and some data collection.
#### What Vaultaire does well
- Encryption it explains. The listing names AES-256-GCM, and its website describes how the pattern becomes a key and how backups are protected. Few vaults publish this much.
- No account, no ads, no tracking. Its privacy label lists no data used to track you, and the listing says there are no ads.
- Free backup. Encrypted iCloud backup is included on the free plan and turned on by default.
- 3 vaults on the free plan , so a decoy plus two more without paying.
- Family plans. Pro for your Apple family, at $49.99 a year or $99.99 for life. Noxium doesn't sell one.
- 31 languages , against Noxium's 16, and import from Files and by drag and drop as well as from Photos.
- A head start. Eight months on the App Store, with ratings and reviews you can read.
#### Where Vaultaire falls short
- A smaller free plan : 100 photos and 10 videos in total, across all vaults.
- PBKDF2 rather than a memory-hard function. 600,000 iterations of PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 is a reasonable, standard choice, but it uses almost no memory, so it is cheaper to run in bulk on graphics cards than Argon2id, which is designed to need a lot of memory for every guess.
- The recovery sentence can be viewed later from the open vault's settings, which Vaultaire's own page notes means anyone who gets into the vault may see it.
- Some data collected. Its privacy label lists data linked to you and data not linked to you; it doesn't say "Data Not Collected".
- Optimized imports by default. Vaultaire's own guide says imports default to an Optimized setting that can convert or downscale photos and videos, with an Original setting you can choose instead.
### How are Vaultaire and Noxium different?
On the big things they match: no account, AES-256-GCM on the device, a 5×5 pattern, decoys, and a free encrypted backup in your own iCloud. The differences are in how the pattern becomes a key, how recovery works, the free plan, price and data collection.
#### How the pattern becomes a key
Noxium stretches your pattern with Argon2id using 64 MiB of memory and 3 passes, and the pattern itself is never stored. Vaultaire uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 with 600,000 iterations and, its site says, keeps the pattern inside an encrypted database in the iOS Keychain. Both are sound designs; Argon2id is the newer standard because the memory it needs makes mass guessing more expensive. For the background, see how encrypted photo vaults work and our pattern lock page.
#### Recovery
Both give you a phrase in case you forget your pattern, and both work on a new iPhone through the iCloud backup. Noxium's is 8 random words from the BIP-39 list (or 6–9 words of your own), shown once at setup and never stored, so it can't be shown again; you can make a new one in Settings. Vaultaire's is a 9-word generated sentence that you can view again later in settings. One is safer if someone gets into your vault; the other is easier if you lose your paper copy. More on ours: recovery phrase .
#### Decoys and panic options
Both open a decoy vault with a second pattern. With Pro, both have a pattern for when you're forced to open the app: Noxium's emergency erase opens a harmless vault and erases the others; Vaultaire's duress vault removes access to the other vaults on that device. Read what a decoy vault is for the limits of both.
#### Free plan and price
Noxium's free plan holds 150 photos, 10 videos and unlimited notes, with 1 decoy vault. Vaultaire's holds 100 photos and 10 videos across up to 3 vaults. For Pro, Vaultaire's yearly plan is $19.99; Noxium's is $17.99. Both sell lifetime Pro for $39.99. Vaultaire's weekly plan is cheaper: $1.99, against Noxium's $2.99. If Noxium Pro ends, you keep full access to view, export and back up everything already in your vault.
#### Privacy label
Noxium has no ads, no accounts and no analytics, and its label is Data Not Collected. Vaultaire lists no tracking but does list data linked to you and data not linked to you.
### Which should you choose?
- Pick Vaultaire if you want 3 vaults without paying, a family plan, the app in a language Noxium doesn't offer yet, or an app with a few months of reviews behind it.
- Pick Noxium if you want a bigger free plan, Argon2id key stretching, a recovery phrase that is never stored, a cheaper yearly Pro, and a Data Not Collected label.
### How do you switch from Vaultaire without losing photos?
Export to Photos, check the copies, import into the new vault, and only then delete anything. Vaultaire says you can export files back into Photos.
- Check your import setting. If photos went into Vaultaire under its Optimized setting, the export can't bring back the original size. Compare a few with the originals if you still have them.
- Export each vault to Photos , one at a time, including any decoy you want to keep. Note how many items each holds.
- Check the copies : counts match, videos play, dates look right.
- Import into Noxium with Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos on, then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
- Wait for Noxium's backup to finish in Settings › iCloud backup .
- Only then delete from Vaultaire, including its iCloud backup if you no longer want it, and cancel Pro in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Exported photos are unencrypted in your library until the new vault imports them. Do the move in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.
Same idea, more room on the free plan
Noxium is free for 150 photos, 10 videos and unlimited notes, with full encrypted iCloud backup and restore.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Is Vaultaire safe?
It encrypts files on the device with AES-256-GCM, needs no account, and its iCloud backup is encrypted before upload. Like any vault, it's only as strong as your pattern, so use a long one.
Is Vaultaire free?
Yes, for up to 3 vaults, 100 photos and 10 videos, with encrypted iCloud backup. Pro starts at $1.99 a week on the US App Store; lifetime is $39.99.
Does Vaultaire need an account?
No. It works without an account, and its backups go to your own iCloud. Noxium works the same way.
What if I forget my Vaultaire pattern?
Use the 9-word recovery sentence from setup. Vaultaire says that if you lose both the pattern and the sentence, nobody can restore the vault.
Vaultaire or Keepsafe?
They're built differently: Vaultaire has no account and backs up to your iCloud; Keepsafe uses an email account and its own cloud. See Vaultaire vs Keepsafe .

# Hidden album vs a photo vault app: which do you need?

URL: https://getnoxium.app/compare/apple-hidden-album
Last updated: 2026-11-15

Compare
## Hidden album vs a photo vault app: which do you need?
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 15 November 2026
Short answer
Apple's Hidden album is free, built in and locked with Face ID, which is enough to keep photos out of casual view. It opens with your iPhone passcode, has no decoy, and syncs to every device on your Apple Account. A photo vault app like Noxium adds a separate code, encryption with a key only you hold, and a decoy for when you're made to unlock.
Most people try the Hidden album first, and for many it's all they need. This page compares it point by point with a dedicated vault app, using Noxium, which we make, as the example. We say plainly where the Hidden album is the better choice. Apple's details come from its own support pages, checked on 15 November 2026; for a closer look at the album alone, read is the iPhone Hidden album private?
### Hidden album vs Noxium at a glance
Source: Apple Support, checked 15 November 2026. Noxium: our published facts.
Noxium Hidden album
Price Free for 150 photos and 10 videos; Pro $2.99/week, $17.99/year or $39.99 once Free, built into Photos
Opens with A pattern on a 5×5 plate, separate from your passcode; Face ID optional Face ID, Touch ID or your iPhone passcode
Encryption AES-256-GCM on the device, key from your pattern The iPhone's own encryption, unlocked by your passcode
Backup Your own iCloud, encrypted before upload iCloud Photos; end-to-end only with Advanced Data Protection
Other devices Separate; iPhone and iPad sync is Pro Hidden photos sync to every device with iCloud Photos on
Decoy Yes, 1 free No
Notes Encrypted notes Photos and videos only
Editing and sharing View, export, share Full Photos editing, search and sharing
If you forget your code Recovery phrase you write down at setup Your iPhone passcode recovery
### What does the Hidden album do well, and where does it fall short?
The Hidden album is the easiest private space on an iPhone. Its limits all come from one fact: it's part of your normal library, behind your normal passcode.
#### What the Hidden album does well
- It's free and already there. Touch and hold a photo, then tap Hide . Nothing to install, nothing to pay.
- Locked by default. Since iOS 16, the Hidden album and Recently Deleted need Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode to open.
- You can hide the album itself. Turn off Settings › Apps › Photos › Show Hidden Album and it disappears from Collections.
- Full quality, full Photos. Hidden photos keep their originals, edits, Live Photos and metadata, and you can edit or share them as usual.
- Backed up with everything else through iCloud Photos, and end-to-end encrypted if you turn on Advanced Data Protection.
#### Where it falls short
- Your passcode opens it. Anyone who knows or has watched your iPhone passcode can open the Hidden album. Face ID is a convenience, not a second lock.
- No decoy. If someone makes you unlock the phone, there's nothing harmless to show instead.
- It spreads to other devices. With iCloud Photos on, hidden photos are on every iPad and Mac signed in to your Apple Account, including a shared family iPad.
- Apple holds the iCloud keys unless you turn on Advanced Data Protection.
- Photos only. There's nowhere for private notes or documents.
### How is a vault app different from the Hidden album?
A vault adds a separate lock and its own encryption key. That changes who can get in, not just who can see a thumbnail.
#### A separate code
Noxium opens with a pattern across a 5×5 plate , which has nothing to do with your iPhone passcode. Someone who knows your passcode can unlock the phone but still can't open the vault.
#### A key only you hold
Every photo, video and note in Noxium is encrypted on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, using a key made from your pattern. Names, dates and places are encrypted too. The Hidden album relies on the iPhone's own encryption, which unlocks with the passcode. See on-device encryption .
#### What happens in iCloud
Hidden photos sit in iCloud Photos with the rest of your library. With standard iCloud protection, Apple can decrypt them; with Advanced Data Protection on, it can't. Noxium's backup is encrypted on the iPhone before upload either way, and goes to its own space in your iCloud, not to iCloud Photos.
#### Decoys
In Noxium, a second pattern opens a separate decoy vault that looks like an ordinary Noxium. The Hidden album has nothing like it. Our guide on decoy vaults explains when that helps.
#### Convenience
The Hidden album wins here. It's free, it's part of Photos, and it keeps your edits, search and sharing. A vault is one more app and one more code to remember.
### Which should you use?
- Use the Hidden album if you only want photos out of your main library and nobody around you knows your passcode. Turn on Advanced Data Protection for end-to-end encrypted iCloud Photos.
- Use a vault app if people around you know your passcode, you share an iPad or Mac, you might be pressured to unlock your phone, or you want notes kept private too.
Many people use both: the Hidden album for things that are merely personal, a vault for things that must stay private. For the full range of options, see every way to hide photos on iPhone .
### How do you move photos from the Hidden album into a vault?
Bring them back into the library, import them into the vault, and then delete them from Photos and from Recently Deleted.
- Open the Hidden album. In Photos, tap Collections , scroll to Utilities › Hidden , tap View Album and unlock it with Face ID or Touch ID.
- Unhide the photos. Touch and hold a photo, then tap Unhide . It goes back to your library at full quality.
- Import them into Noxium with Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos on, so it offers to delete them from Photos after import.
- Empty Recently Deleted in Collections › Utilities › Recently Deleted . Until you do, the copies are still on the phone and in iCloud Photos.
- Check Noxium's backup in Settings › iCloud backup .
Watch out
Unhidden photos appear in your main library until you import and delete them. Do it in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.
A vault with its own key
Noxium opens with a pattern only you know, not your iPhone passcode. Free for 150 photos, 10 videos and 1 decoy vault.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Is the Hidden album as safe as a photo vault app?
Not against someone who knows your iPhone passcode, because the passcode opens it. Against someone just scrolling your phone, it's fine. A vault adds a separate code and its own encryption.
Can someone see my Hidden album with my passcode?
Yes. The Hidden album unlocks with Face ID, Touch ID or the iPhone passcode, so anyone with the passcode can open it.
Do hidden photos sync to iCloud?
Yes, with iCloud Photos on. They stay hidden on your other devices too. They're end-to-end encrypted in iCloud only if you turn on Advanced Data Protection.
Do I need a vault app if I use Advanced Data Protection?
It depends on who you're worried about. Advanced Data Protection keeps Apple out of your iCloud Photos, but anyone with your passcode can still open the Hidden album on the phone.
Will photos I move into a vault still be in iCloud Photos?
Only until you delete them from Photos and empty Recently Deleted. After that, the only copies are in the vault and its own encrypted backup.

- Apple Support, How to turn on Advanced Data Protection for iCloud .

## Calculator# Hide Photos review: how it compares with Noxium

Short answer
Calculator# disguises itself as a calculator and packs in a lot: photos, documents, a password manager, notes, contacts, cloud backup to iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive, and email password recovery. Its listing doesn't name any encryption, and the free version has ads. Pick Calculator# for its disguise and extras; pick Noxium if you want named encryption and no ads or tracking.
Calculator# Hide Photos Videos has been on the App Store since November 2016 and has 28,955 US ratings at 4.4 stars. It's one of the best-known "calculator" vaults: the app looks like a working calculator, and the right code opens the hidden space. This review covers what it does well and where it falls short, from its App Store listing checked on 15 November 2026, and compares it with Noxium. We make Noxium, so weigh what we say about our own app accordingly.

### What does Calculator# do well, and where does it fall short?
Calculator# does more than almost any vault, at a low price. What its listing doesn't say is how any of it is protected.
#### What Calculator# does well
- A convincing disguise. It works as a calculator, so a quick look at the phone shows nothing unusual.
- Many lock options: a calculator code, PIN, password, pattern, or Touch ID / Face ID.
- Far more than photos. Documents, audio, notes, to-dos, secret contacts and a password manager and wallet, all in one place.
- Backup to the cloud you choose : iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive.
- Email recovery if you forget your password.
- Hack Monitor logs wrong password attempts, a panic switch jumps to another app, and a disguise mode shows a fake crash message.
- Cheap. $4.99 a year removes ads and limits. It's actively updated (30 October 2026) and works on iPad.
#### Where Calculator# falls short
- No encryption named. The listing talks about hiding, locking and password-protecting, but never says how files are encrypted, or whether the cloud backups are.
- A disguise isn't encryption. A calculator front keeps out a casual glance. It does nothing if someone gets at the files another way, or knows what the app is.
- No decoy space. The panic switch jumps to another app, which helps against someone looking over your shoulder but not someone who makes you open the vault.
- Ads and tracking. The free version shows ads, and its privacy label lists data used to track you.
- Email recovery cuts both ways. It's a safety net, but anyone with access to that email account may be able to use it too.
### How are Calculator# and Noxium different?
Calculator# hides things behind a disguise and many features. Noxium does fewer things and encrypts all of them with a key only your pattern makes.
#### Encryption
Noxium encrypts every photo, video and note on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, with a key made from your pattern through Argon2id. Names, dates and places are encrypted too. Calculator#'s listing names no cipher. If that matters to you, ask the developer; our guide on how encrypted photo vaults work explains what to ask.
#### Backup
Calculator# lets you back up to iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive. Its listing doesn't say whether those backups are encrypted first. Noxium backs up only encrypted data, to your own iCloud, and restores on a new iPhone with your pattern; see encrypted iCloud backup .
#### Disguise
Calculator# is a working calculator. Noxium Pro can change its Home Screen icon to a Calculator, Notes or Weather lookalike , and hides vault content in the app switcher and in screen recordings, but it opens to its own lock screen, not a working calculator. For other apps with this disguise, see calculator vault apps .
#### When someone makes you open it
Noxium's second pattern opens a separate decoy vault, 1 on the free plan, and Pro adds an emergency erase pattern. Calculator#'s listing offers a panic switch and a fake crash message instead. See what a decoy vault is .
#### Price and privacy
Calculator#'s yearly plan is $4.99. Noxium's free plan has no ads and holds 150 photos, 10 videos and unlimited notes, with full backup; Noxium Pro is $17.99 a year or $39.99 once. Noxium has no ads, no accounts and no analytics, and its privacy label is Data Not Collected.
### Which should you choose?
- Pick Calculator# if a working calculator disguise matters most, or you want one app for photos, documents, passwords and contacts, with backup to Dropbox or Google Drive.
- Pick Noxium if you want encryption that's named and documented, an encrypted backup in your own iCloud, a decoy vault, and no ads or tracking.
### How do you switch from Calculator# without losing photos?
Move the photos back to your Photos library, check them, import them into the new vault, and only then delete them from Calculator#.
- Count what you have in each Calculator# album, and note any documents or passwords you'll need to move elsewhere.
- Get the photos and videos out of Calculator#, back to your Photos library from inside the app, or to a computer with the Wi-Fi transfer its listing describes.
- Check them in Photos: counts match, videos play, photos open at full size.
- Import into Noxium with Settings › App settings › Offer to delete from Photos on, then empty Recently Deleted in Photos.
- Check the backup in Noxium's Settings › iCloud backup .
- Only then delete from Calculator#, remove any cloud backups you made with it, and cancel the subscription in Settings › [your name] › Subscriptions .
Watch out
Exported photos sit unencrypted in your Photos library until the new vault imports them. Do the move in one sitting, on a phone only you are using.
Encryption, not just a disguise
Noxium encrypts everything on your iPhone with AES-256-GCM. Pro can also change its icon to a Calculator, Notes or Weather lookalike.

### Questions people ask
Is Calculator# Hide Photos safe?
It hides files behind a working calculator and a code, and it's actively updated. Its listing doesn't name any encryption, and its privacy label lists data used to track you. See are photo vault apps safe?
How much does Calculator# cost?
It's free with ads and limits. A year without ads costs $4.99 on the US App Store, and a Premium Features Pack is another $4.99.
What if I forget my Calculator# password?
Its listing says you can recover it through the email address you registered. Make sure that email account is secure, because it's a way into the vault.
Do calculator vault apps really hide photos?
They hide the app's purpose from a quick look. Whether the photos are protected depends on encryption, which a disguise doesn't provide by itself. Many vaults, including Noxium Pro, offer a lookalike icon on top of encryption.
Does Calculator# back up my photos?
Yes, if you set it up. Its listing says it can back up to iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive or OneDrive.

### What does Hide it Pro do well, and where does it fall short?
Hide it Pro keeps things simple and makes it easy to get your files back out. What its listing leaves unsaid is how the files are protected.
#### What Hide it Pro does well
- Simple and long-running. More than 13 years on the App Store, rated 4.7 by nearly 25,000 people.
- Albums you can rename and give their own thumbnail, with GIF support, a built-in viewer and player, and moving between albums.
- Easy to get files out. Unhide back to the gallery, or export everything over USB in one tap. That makes leaving, or keeping your own copy, painless.
- Tricks for prying eyes. A fake crash screen, automatic locking when you leave the app, and an escape code that opens the app looking empty.
- No tracking. Its privacy label lists no data used to track you.
- No subscription unless you want cloud storage. The app itself is free.
#### Where Hide it Pro falls short
- No encryption named. The listing describes hiding photos behind a lock screen but doesn't say whether, or how, files are encrypted.
- Backup costs extra for real space. Cloud storage is in its own cloud, and unlimited space is a monthly subscription. The listing doesn't say whether that backup is encrypted.
- Paid password reset. Recovery is sold separately for $4.99, and the listing doesn't explain how the reset works.
- Not updated since 11 January 2026 , and the app is in English only.
### How are Hide it Pro and Noxium different?
Hide it Pro is about hiding and easy export. Noxium is about encryption you can rely on and a backup only you can open.

Noxium encrypts every photo, video and note on the iPhone with AES-256-GCM, using a key made from your pattern through Argon2id; names, dates and places are encrypted too. Hide it Pro's listing names no cipher. Read on-device encryption for why this matters if someone gets at the files another way.

Noxium's backup is free, encrypted on the iPhone first, and stored in your own iCloud; on a new iPhone you draw your pattern and it restores. Hide it Pro's escape code makes the app look empty. Noxium's second pattern opens a decoy vault with photos you choose, which can look more natural than an empty app. Pro adds an emergency erase pattern .
#### Forgetting your code
Noxium has no reset by anyone. You write down a recovery phrase at setup, and it opens your vault on this iPhone or a new one. Hide it Pro sells a password reset for $4.99.
#### Price and privacy
Hide it Pro's Cloud Storage is $9.99. Noxium's free plan includes 150 photos, 10 videos, unlimited notes and full backup; Pro is $17.99 a year or $39.99 once. Both report no tracking; Noxium's label is Data Not Collected.

Noxium is built for photos and videos, with encrypted notes alongside, and imports HEIC, ProRAW and Live Photos and exports them in full quality with original dates. If most of what you protect is documents, Secret Photo Vault's viewers are more useful; if it's photos, Noxium keeps them closer to the originals.

Is Secret Photo Vault safe?

Does Secret Photo Vault back up to iCloud?
Not according to its listing, which says your data is stored only on your device. Copy files off with Wi-Fi or USB transfer if you want a backup.
Is Secret Photo Vault the same as Keepsafe or SPV?
No. Keepsafe's App Store name is "Secret Photo Vault: Keepsafe", and SPV is "SPV - Secret Photo Vault". This page is about "Secret Photo Vault Lock Photos".
How much is Secret Photo Vault Pro?
$6.99, once, on the US App Store in November 2026.
What if I forget my Secret Photo Vault password?
If you set up the optional security question, you can reset it with that. If not, don't delete the app; read our guide to a forgotten vault password first.

# Calculator vault apps: how they work and what they hide

URL: https://getnoxium.app/guides/calculator-vault-apps
Last updated: 2026-11-16

Guide · Choosing a vault
## Calculator vault apps: how they work and what they hide
By Inertia Projects · Last updated 16 November 2026
Short answer
A calculator vault app looks and works like a calculator, but typing a secret code and = opens a hidden store of photos and videos. The disguise stops a quick glance at your Home Screen. It doesn't stop someone who checks Settings, and many of these apps name no encryption, show ads or track you, so read the listing before you trust one.
Calculator vaults are some of the most common photo hiders on the App Store. This guide explains how the disguise works, what it protects and what it doesn't, and what three calculator vaults say about themselves on their App Store listings, checked on 16 November 2026. We make Noxium, a photo vault with an optional calculator lookalike icon, so we say where it fits and where it doesn't.
### How does a calculator vault app work?
It opens as a working calculator. A code you choose, typed on the keypad and followed by =, opens the vault instead of showing a result.
- The icon and first screen look like a calculator. Anyone who opens it sees sums work as normal.
- Your code is the key. At setup you pick a number, such as a PIN. Typing it and pressing = opens the hidden part.
- Inside is a gallery. You import photos and videos from Photos, and many apps offer to delete the originals for you.
- Extras vary. Some add decoy codes, a panic switch, notes, passwords, contacts or cloud backup.
The disguise is a social tool: it makes the app look boring to someone scrolling through your phone. Whether the photos are encrypted is a separate question, and the calculator screen says nothing about it. For the difference between hiding and encrypting, see how encrypted photo vaults work .
### What do popular calculator vaults say about themselves?
Here is what three calculator vaults state on their US App Store listings. None of their listings names an encryption method.
Source: each app's US App Store listing, checked 16 November 2026.
App Ratings Last update Privacy label Backup Paid options
Calculator# Hide Photos Videos 28,955 · 4.4★ 30 Oct 2026 Data Used to Track You iCloud, Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive $4.99 yearly; $4.99 pack
Calculator Lock - Secure Vault 6,629 · 4.6★ 20 Dec 2024 Data Used to Track You Not in listing $1.99 a week to $29.99 lifetime; Remove Ads $3.99
Private Photos (Calculator%) 457 · 4.1★ 24 Jun 2021 Data Not Collected None; "stored locally on your device" $0.99 to lift the photo limit
- Calculator# is the busiest: photos, videos, documents, a password manager, contacts, notes and to-dos, Wi-Fi transfer, cloud backup, and a "Panic Switch, Disguise Mode & Hack Monitoring". It unlocks with a calculator code, PIN, password, pattern, Touch ID or Face ID. Our Calculator# review goes through it point by point.
- Calculator Lock hides photos and videos, contacts, notes and passwords. Its in-app purchases include "Remove Ads", which suggests the free version shows ads, and it hasn't been updated since December 2024.
- Private Photos (Calculator%) is simple and collects no data, but it was last updated in June 2021. Its listing says photos you import must be deleted from the Photos app by hand.
### What does the calculator disguise protect against?
It protects against a casual look. Someone swiping through your Home Screen, or opening the app, sees a calculator.
- A partner, child or friend holding your phone for a minute is unlikely to try a code on a calculator.
- A photo popping up in the wrong place. Once you delete the originals from the Photos app, they no longer show up in Memories, widgets or Photos search.
### What doesn't a calculator vault protect against?
Anyone who looks at the phone's lists of apps, or at the files themselves. The disguise lives only on the Home Screen.
- The App Store. Your list of purchased apps shows each app by its full store name, and a name like "Calculator Lock - Secure Vault" gives the game away.
- iPhone Storage. Settings › General › iPhone Storage lists every app and how much space it uses. A "calculator" holding gigabytes of videos stands out.
- Someone who knows the trick. Calculator vaults are well known. A second calculator next to Apple's own is a hint.
- A copy of the phone's storage. If the files aren't encrypted, anyone who can read the app's storage can see them. None of the three listings above names any encryption.
- A lost phone. An app with no backup loses everything with the phone. Private Photos (Calculator%) says its data stays only on the device.
- The app itself. Two of the three apps above carry the "Data Used to Track You" privacy label. A vault that tracks you is an odd place for private photos. See are photo vault apps safe? for what each label means.
### How do you check a calculator vault before you trust it?
Read four things on its App Store page: encryption, privacy label, backup and last update. It takes two minutes.
- Search the description for "encrypt". Look for a named method, such as AES-256. "Secure" and "protected" alone don't say how.
- Scroll to App Privacy . "Data Not Collected" is best. "Data Used to Track You" means the app shares data for tracking.
- Find out where backups go. Your own iCloud, the developer's cloud, or nowhere. If it's the developer's cloud, look for whether it's encrypted before upload.
- Check Version History . An app not updated in over a year may not keep up with new iOS versions.
- Test before you move everything. Add a few photos, close the app, and open it again with your code. Only then delete originals from Photos, and empty Recently Deleted .
### What are the alternatives to a calculator vault?
Pick by what you're hiding from. For a quick glance, iPhone's own tools may be enough. For anyone who might dig, you want encryption.
- iPhone's Hidden album. Free and built in, locked with Face ID or your passcode. Anyone who knows your passcode can open it. See Hidden album vs a photo vault app .
- Lock the Photos app. On iOS 18 and later, touch and hold the Photos icon and tap Require Face ID . Our guide to locking photos with Face ID has the steps.
- An encrypted vault with a disguise option. Noxium encrypts every photo, video and note with AES-256-GCM, with a key made from a pattern you draw. With Pro, you can change its Home Screen icon to a Calculator, Notes or Weather lookalike; see custom app icons . It opens with a pattern, not a calculator, and the name under the icon still reads "Noxium".
More apps, with and without disguises, are side by side in our full photo vault comparison .
Encryption first, disguise second
Noxium encrypts photos, videos and notes on your iPhone before they're saved. Pro adds plain-looking icons, including a Calculator lookalike.
Download on the App Store
Available on the App Store for iPhone and iPad.
### Questions people ask
Are calculator vault apps safe?
They're safe from a quick look, not from a determined one. Check that the listing names encryption, that the privacy label isn't "Data Used to Track You", and that it was updated in the last year.
Can someone find photos hidden in a calculator app?
They can find the app: your App Store purchases list it by its full name, and iPhone Storage shows how much it holds. Seeing the photos still takes your code, or access to the files if they aren't encrypted.
Do calculator vault apps encrypt photos?
Some may, but none of the three we checked says so on its listing. If an app doesn't name an encryption method, assume the photos are only hidden.
What happens if I forget my calculator code?
It depends on the app: some use an email or security question, and some have no way back. Don't delete the app first; read our guide to a forgotten vault password .
Is there a calculator vault without ads?
Yes. Private Photos (Calculator%) lists no ads and collects no data, but it hasn't been updated since 2021. Our list of vaults without subscriptions or ads has more.
